Deaths of newborns have risen by more than 80 per cent among the most vulnerable people across sub-Saharan Africa in the wake of global aid cuts, including by the UK and US.

Data covering more than three million refugee women across 20 nations, given exclusively to The Independent, shows that neonatal mortality – deaths within the first 28 days after birth – rose by 81 per cent between 2025 and 2026. That is a rise from 3.1 to 5.6 deaths per 1,000 live births, according to the UN refugee agency (UNHCR).

While the agency makes clear the data does not establish the cause, or that aid cuts were the sole factor behind the rise, it does show that indicators of child survival are worsening. Deaths within the first year of life have also increased by 111 per cent, from 8.3 to 17.5 deaths per 1,000 live births. Mortality for children under five also rose by 50 per cent.

Through an analysis of this data, plus that from other UN agencies, charities and NGOs, The Independent can reveal a grim picture of maternal and child health across Africa as sweeping cuts to international aid and the lifesaving programmes it funded begin to bite.

More than 11 million people have lost access to essential sexual and reproductive health and protection services, according to the UN Population Fund (UNFPA).

Almost 1,100 UNFPA health facilities and mobile clinics have been forced to close, while a further 727 are operating with reduced staff, limited hours or shortages of medicines and supplies.

Nearly 6,000 healthcare workers, including frontline staff and midwives, have lost their jobs.

There are increasing fears among those working in the development sector that years of progress in reducing maternal and newborn deaths could be reversed by the steep decline in international aid.

open image in gallery A children's hospital in the Central African Republic ( Bel Trew/The Independent )

“Global maternal mortality trends already show us where women’s lives are most at risk, and sub-Saharan Africa remains at the centre of this crisis,” said Dr Mitchell Sangma, a health advisor at Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF).

“Countries depend heavily on external humanitarian and health system support to keep essential services running. When those lifelines are cut without health authorities stepping up, the consequences are predictable. I fear even more maternal deaths will happen quietly in communities, unseen and unrecorded.”

In Nigeria, 386 health facilities and mobile clinics – a significant number of which deal with maternal health – closed during 2025 and early 2026, cutting off care for around 380,000 people. Meanwhile, more than 100,000 people lost access to essential health services in the Central African Republic.

Both countries are featured in Hard Labour , the new documentary for Independent TV, by our chief international correspondent Bel Trew. It exposes how efforts to stop women and babies dying in childbirth have been blunted, with aid cuts playing a significant role.

open image in gallery A refugee from Sudan at a health facility in the Central African Republic ( Bel Trew/The Independent )

Significant progress in tackling preventable maternal mortality across the globe had seen the rate decline by 40 per cent in the last two decades, but this had started to slow, even before the slashing of billions of pounds from global aid.

According to the WHO, the average annual decline in global maternal mortality rate was 1.5 per cent between 2013 and 2023, a figure significantly below the 2.6 per cent recorded between 2000 and 2010.

The benchmark is the UN Sustainable Development Goal, laid out in 2015, for the global maternal mortality rate to fall below 70 deaths per 100,000 live births by 2030.

The latest data puts the global maternal mortality rate at 197 per 100,000 live births, with a number of nations significantly above that.

Seventy-five per cent of deaths are due to either severe bleeding, infections, high blood pressure during pregnancy, complications from delivery, or unsafe abortion.

The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), which works with more than 100 countries, has projected that official development assistance for health could fall by between 29 and 46 per cent between 2024 and 2026, equivalent to between $5bn and $8bn.

Funding for population and reproductive health, including HIV and sexually transmitted infection programmes, is expected to fall by as much as 54 per cent.

A study published in March estimated that the Trump administration's aid cuts could increase maternal mortality by an average of 45 per cent across Burkina Faso, the Central African Republic, Chad, Mali, Niger and Nigeria.

The researchers projected around 1,000 additional maternal deaths per 100,000 live births across the six countries within a single year.

"The world has made remarkable progress in reducing maternal deaths over the past two decades, proving that these deaths are not inevitable when women can access quality healthcare,” said Sarah Shaw, of advocacy group MSI Reproductive Choices.

“But across many of the countries where MSI Reproductive Choices works, cuts to global health funding, alongside conflict and displacement are making it harder for women to access essential reproductive services.”

In Somalia, CARE International says that, since January, it has been forced to close 50 of the 80 health and nutrition centres it supported because of funding shortfalls, with another 15 due to shut by October.

They are already seeing a spike in severe malnutrition – in a country that has one of the highest maternal mortality ratios in the world.

"This is a devastating blow to families who rely on us for basic healthcare and lifesaving nutrition,” said Ummy Dubow, CARE's Somalia country director. “When these centres shut down, pregnant women and young children pay the ultimate price.”

Save The Children estimates that Somalia also faces a shortage of around 20,000 midwives, while some hospital staff have faced up to a 90 per cent reduction in salaries, which has left midwives around the country effectively volunteering to keep services running.

Globally, the World Health Organisation (WHO) has said the shortfall of midwives could reach between 690,000 and 830,000 by 2030 – with Africa bearing the brunt of the burden as it will carry 46 per cent of the deficit.

The findings have renewed calls across the political spectrum for the UK, and the government under new prime minister Andy Burnham, to reverse cuts to the overseas aid budget, which will fall from 0.5 to 0.3 per cent of Gross National Income through to 2029.

Nine African countries are set to see their UK bilateral aid cut by more than 80 per cent, while overall bilateral UK aid to African countries is set to fall from £1.6bn to under £700m.

Sarah Champion, chair of parliament’s International Development Committee and a Labour MP, said: "The Trump administration has politicised maternal and sexual health. Not only has it dramatically cut funding, it has also orchestrated a chilling effect on other donor countries.

“It is the babies and mothers in the poorest countries who are bearing the brunt of his ideology. The UK has been very clear on its focus on women and girls, this is the right approach; but these stark finding show that is just not the reality on the ground.

“Unless the international community comes together to support low-income countries, I fear the situation will only get worse.”

Andrew Mitchell, a former international development secretary and Conservative MP for Sutton Coldfield added: "These figures lay bare the appalling effects of these cuts and the damage to the most vulnerable as well as to Britain's reputation.

"Surely it is not too much to ask that a new prime minister looks again at this and puts right the errors of judgment of [Boris] Johnson and [Keir] Starmer."

Monica Harding, the Liberal Democrat spokesperson for international development, called on Mr Burnham to take decisive action to prevent “further tragic loss of life”.

”The government cannot claim to be empowering women and girls around the world while pushing on with immoral and strategically illiterate aid cuts - gutting the basic healthcare, life-saving protection, and maternal services keeping them and their babies alive,” she said.

It was early 2025 when the Trump administration abruptly dismantled the US Agency for International Development (USAID), the world's largest provider of humanitarian and development aid. It cancelled thousands of health and aid programmes almost overnight.

The speed of the cuts left UN agencies and charities with little time to find alternative funding or wind down services safely. Then came the announcement that UK aid cuts would follow, in order to help pay for an increase in defence funding.

Internal USAID modelling found the funding freeze could affect services for 16.8 million pregnant women each year and eliminate postnatal care for 11.3 million newborns during their first two days of life.

France, Germany and the Netherlands have all announced further reductions to their aid budgets, with several governments citing the need to increase defence spending in response to growing security threats.

Aid organisations have warned that women and newborns are likely to bear the heaviest burden, as maternal healthcare, emergency obstetric services and reproductive health programmes are among those most affected.

Earlier this year, projections published in The Lancet suggested that reductions in foreign aid could contribute to 23 million additional deaths across 93 low- and middle-income countries by 2030.

“We know how to prevent the majority of maternal deaths. What we need is political will and international co-operation,” said Samy Ahmar, Head of Global Health at Save the Children UK.

George Ayres, from Plan International UK, added: “These deaths are preventable. Every cut to aid is putting more mothers and babies at risk. World leaders must act now to protect maternal health and ensure mothers can access the care they need.”

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Kerr wins by a mile: Scot claims Commonwealth gold to emulate Bannister
News.content:
“It means everything – absolutely incredible,” said Kerr, who joined the rendition of Flower of Scotland before closing his eyes to soak up the moment in a stadium where he had competed as a child in even the shot put.

“To do it in front of a Scottish crowd, where I learned how to race, doesn’t get any better,” he added. “I came here week after week growing up as a kid. This was the championship of my season with the world indoors and going after the record. This was on the calendar before any of that. I think a British crowd deserved more from me and I owed them that.”

Of the tactics compared to his world record, where he had to hold an even pace throughout, Kerr stressed the importance of staying calm and not being tempted into pushing too soon. “London was a big stress, pushing my body to the extreme limit,” he said. “Doing a championship race is a nice clean slate; using your brain instead of your body. It’s how I love to race.

“When you’re running that slow, your job is not to waste energy and I did that. I knew an opportunity would open up. Then it was about staying awake and alive and trying to get some space. felt like I had plenty of gears left in me.”

Kerr had emerged to a huge home ovation and, with the Proclaimers booming out as the runners completed the first two laps, he was content to stay in the pack even as Myers followed. There was then only one brief moment of concern as the runners began gathering themselves during the penultimate lap and Kerr became momentarily boxed in.

News.title: Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid
News.content:
Manchester United 2 Atletico Madrid 1

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

News.title: Richarlison grabs last-gasp winner for 10-man Spurs in fiery Chelsea friendly
News.content:
Tottenham Hotspur 2 Chelsea 1

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.



Just as the game appeared to be heading to penalties, Richarlison scored on the follow-up after Jamie Donley hit the post in the final few seconds of added time.

News.title: Massage guns vs compression boots: Which is better for muscle recovery?
News.content:
Looking after your body is no longer just about getting a good workout in; it’s ensuring that you’re properly recuperating afterwards, too. Luckily, in 2026, there is a huge range of products designed to aid recovery.

In fact, the recovery tech boom is playing a big role in the growth of the sports technology market overall. Estimates show it’s projected to grow from $39.6 billion in 2026 to $192.3 billion by 2034.

Two of the most popular products in this category are massage guns and compression boots. Both claim to ease muscle soreness and help you bounce back to training sooner, but they sit at very different price points. You can pick up a basic gun from around £40, whereas the cheapest boots we tested were £300. But which method is actually better for improving workout recovery?

Massage guns can help to improve flexibility in older muscles

Massage guns work by delivering repeated percussion and vibration to one specific area, which helps improve the mobility and flexibility of a specific muscle. In turn, this can make your muscles feel less tense and stiff. These gadgets can be used before and after workout sessions.

While useful for all ages, massage guns can be helpful for anyone looking to improve range of movement, ease muscle stiffness and boost blood flow – whether exercising or not.

“It will help temporarily improve your mobility so that you feel like you’ve got a bit more flexibility in that muscle,” explains Jonathan Wreaves, clinical physiologist at preventative health clinic Viavi.

But how do they actually work?

Most massage guns offer a revolutions per minute (RPM) range, which refers to how many times the massage head moves back and forth every minute. This tends to be somewhere between 1200 and 3500. The lower range is ideal for gentle massage and warming up, while a higher RPM is better for targeting bigger muscle groups and more intense tightness.

News.title: Battle rages over access to new ‘miracle’ HIV drug
News.content:
For the first time in the four-decade fight against HIV there is a “miracle” drug that can all but eliminate the risk of infection, but in the Latin American countries where it was tested almost no one can get it.

Trials show that Lenacapavir, made by Gilead Sciences, is almost 100 per cent effective in preventing HIV infection. With just two shots a year, those taking it will avoid contracting the virus even when frequently exposed.

The drug, which many believe could bring an end to the global HIV pandemic, costs $14,000 a dose in the United States. Gilead has agreed to licence generic versions of the pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) medication at around $40 a dose in 120 low-and middle-income countries, but almost all of Latin America is excluded.

Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru are among those with serious HIV epidemics that are shut out, despite having run some of the clinical trials that proved the drug works.

Their status as “upper-middle income countries” means they are too rich to qualify for the cut price generic version and yet they remain too poor to pay the US price.

News.title: Senior dating: a guide to finding love later in life
News.content:
Whether you’re a widow, widower or divorcee, the thought of online dating in later life can feel daunting. However, more and more people are turning to the internet to find romance. Roughly 16 per cent of UK adults are using online dating services to meet a partner, according to Statista. Among them, there are lots of singles over 50 using dating sites.

So here’s how to navigate your senior dating online, with expert advice from psychologist and dating coach Dr Pam Spurr, and sex and relationship coach Angela Vossen.

How do I know if I'm ready to date again as a senior?

Coming out of any relationship is hard. If you’re hoping to date after a divorce, bereavement or break up, it can take a long time to feel ready to date again. Dr Spurr advises taking your time.

“Many people feel bruised, even traumatised, after coming out of a long-term relationship or having been bereaved,” she explains. “Your feelings naturally vary from day to day about whether you're ready to get back out to look for love – or even for fun. A crucial factor is if you've come to the point where you have more good days compared to bad days”.

Dr Spurr explains that good days are the days on which you feel more optimistic about life generally, and you find your thoughts turning to meeting someone new. “That's an important sign that you are healing,” she says. “However, if you're still feeling deeply insecure or are riddled with self-doubt about your worthiness, take your time. When you feel worthy, you will find someone worthy of you”.

Feeling heartbroken? Learn how to get over a break up

How to start senior dating online

If you’re new to online dating, it can feel intimidating at first. The secret is taking things step by step so that you do things at your own pace. The first step, however, should be choosing a senior dating site that will help match you with like-minded people. This will narrow your search and ensure your dating experience is more successful.

Step 1: Create an online profile

Once you’ve decided on a dating site or app and signed up, you’ll be asked to write a dating profile. This should reflect who you are along with your passions, values and what you seek in a partner.

Try to be authentic rather than creating a fantasy version of yourself. If you exaggerate your accomplishments, your date will only feel deceived once they get to know you. Likewise, don’t be tempted to use a photo of yourself from 10 years ago.

What are you waiting for? |  Single and looking to find true love? Sign up today for Telegraph Dating and join more than 220,000 like-minded people. Join today

Step 2: Spark meaningful chats with potential dates

Once you have signed up to a senior dating site and created a profile, you will be free to start looking at other people’s profiles and sending messages to anyone that catches your attention. But how can you initiate a conversation after an introduction?

“When messaging people on dating sites, ask open-ended questions to spark meaningful chats,” says Angela. A good example would be, ‘I can see you enjoy travel. What place have you always wanted to visit but haven’t yet?’ or “tell me more about your love of tennis? Did you watch the US Open?” If things go really well and the chat seems to flow naturally, you may decide to organise a phone chat or ask them out on a date. An initial chat over the phone can help gauge how well you get on and how easily the conversation flows. If this goes well, meeting in person may feel less nerve wracking and a little less ‘blind’.

Step 3: Prioritise your safety

“While most people are well intentioned online, it’s important to protect your safety,” advises Ms Vossen. “Keep personal details private (like where you live or your social media profiles) until you’ve met in person and built trust”. You should also arrange first dates in public places, share your plans with a friend, and trust your instincts if something feels off.

If the first date or two doesn’t quite hit the mark, try not to be too disappointed and remember that you can say no to another date. Ms Vossen says: “Be patient – online dating takes time, but with practice, you’ll gain confidence and enjoy the journey”.

Traditional ways to meet senior singles

Of course, couples continue to meet in a manner that predates online dating sites. If you’re keen to join the older dating scene but find the online world overwhelming, there are plenty of ways to meet people in real life.

1. Holidays and group trips

We are often our best selves on holiday, so it’s the ideal place to find a single senior woman or to meet men if the opportunity presents itself. Why not organise a trip on which you meet new people while doing what you love, whether that’s cycling, walking, sightseeing or just travelling around a new part of the world. There are many escorted tours that cater to specific age groups and interests. They also take away the stress of organising a trip yourself.

“An organised holiday or trip can be a great place to meet someone new and there are many organisations offering these for the over 50s,” says Dr Spur. “A word of caution though, you can spend a lot of money and there's no guarantee that you will meet that special person. However, if it's a place you've wanted to travel to then go with the mindset that you're going to have a great trip. If you meet someone, that's an added bonus”.

2. Activities and social groups

Whether you enjoy walking, reading or volunteering, taking up a new hobby or joining a social group is a great way to enhance your social life and increase your chances of meeting a new romantic interest.

“Joining a club or taking up a hobby can be a fantastic way of meeting singles who enjoy the same pastimes,” says Dr Spur. “You're doing an activity you enjoy knowing that there might also be someone there that will catch your eye”.

If you do meet someone that you’re interested in at a social event, Dr Spur advises starting with a simple ‘hello’ and an easy question such as how long they've been doing that particular activity or hobby. “This can open-up a friendly conversation that might lead to flirting down the line,” she says.

Start online dating for seniors today

Whichever way you decide to start looking for love, approach it in a way that you feel comfortable with. Signing up to an online dating service is a great way to meet other seniors. Remember, it’s never too late to begin a new chapter.

Sports.title: Ex-Man City captain Andy Morrison, 56, in positive health update as he returns to commentary after devastating diagnosis
Sports.content:
FORMER Manchester City captain Andy Morrison has issued a positive update on his condition after being diagnosed with Ramsay Hunt Syndrome.

The 56-year-old was diagnosed with the rare neurological disorder at the start of the year.



A few months later he revealed that his recovery would take a “long, long time” but insisted he was trying to remain positive.

And in his latest update, Morrison declared that he took a big step forward this week by returning to commentary.



The ex-defender covered the pre-season friendly between Man City and Inter Milan – which saw the Premier League giants lose on penalties.

In a social media video, Morrison said: “Evening everyone. Just a quick update after the first day back working at City with the matchday live team, which I thoroughly enjoyed.



“It was fantastic to be back. Felt the voice was strong enough to go back and do co-commentary today.

“That’s my first time back in five-and-a-half months. I really appreciate all the support and working with Ali Mann, who makes it very easy.

“An enjoyable game. I struggled with a few words, a few names, but nothing too bad.

“I did struggle with (Ryan) McAidoo. Could have a player there by the way, watch this space.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“There was enough there to think he could be the next one on the conveyor belt, hugely impressive in the second-half.”

The former City captain went on to add: “Birthday yesterday, that was a great day with grandkids and family.

“I had a specialist on Wednesday and it was really positive, he was really delighted and amazed at the progress I had made, from House-Brackmann (nerve grading scale) six to a four and he is really positive that within a year I’ll get my eye back and be able to blink, so I won’t have to tape it down at night.

“I still have to take juice to swallow and I have no taste in the side of my mouth and the whole side of the face is numb, so I have to drink through a straw still.



“He wasn’t sure just how much that would progress because it’s still really weak. But if sucking through a straw is worst case scenario then so be it. I won’t be posting now because I won’t see a specialist for another three months.

“A really good day and it just felt great to be back doing something when that seemed a million miles away.

“I didn’t get out of bed for four weeks and couldn’t speak for a month. I had some really dark days in this conservatory but I stayed positive and this too shall pass, everything passes, good or bad, everything comes and goes and sometimes you just have to dig in and get through it. But thanks for listening and see you all soon.”

Ramsay Hunt Syndrome is a neurological disorder caused by a virus in the facial nerve.

Morrison signed for Man City from Huddersfield Town in 1998 and went on to feature in the side that won the play-offs to the old Division One during the 1998-99 campaign.

He also played for the likes of Plymouth Argyle, Blackburn Rovers and Blackpool, along with Crystal Palace and Sheffield United on loan.

After hanging up his boots, he went on to become a manager.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso welcomes Mykhailo Mudryk back to Chelsea after 4-year doping ban cut short but admits Blues future unclear
Sports.content:
XABI ALONSO is ready to welcome Mykhailo Mudryk with open arms after the end of his doping ban.

The Chelsea winger, 25, saw his four-year ban cut short this week after the FA and the World Anti-Doping Agency resolved their disciplinary process against him following an appeal.



Mudryk tested positive for a of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance, in 2024 and was slapped with a four year ban which he appealed with the Court of Arbitration for Sport this year.

The £62million forward has always maintained he never intentionally took the substance and changes to testing processes mean that, had the sample been taken today he would not have been reported as failing a drugs test.



Alonso, who had not expected to be working with Mudryk at Chelsea, confirmed the winger will join his squad for the next leg of their pre-season tour, in Hong Kong – despite the fact they have not spoken yet.

He said: “We are happy for him, especially for him, because probably we are not able to understand what he has been through in this time and how does he feel at the moment with the things that he had to cope with.

“We want that he feels part of a team, because he has been training on his own for a long time, and that we have the support from everyone, from the club, from the team-mates, from the staff, and for sure it will take time.

“Once he is with us, we will see how things develop.

“He is coming to Hong Kong, but I haven’t spoken to him yet.”

While many at Chelsea are excited to have Mudryk back, there is yet to be any clarity on his future at the club. He has a contract which runs for another five years, to 2031, but no decision has been made regarding his place in the squad for this season so far.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Alonso added: “We need to see, it’s too early to tell, to see how he is in terms of fitness, in terms of this game time that you need to be involved again, so it’s still early to tell.

“We were not expecting to have this great news at this moment, so we are very happy. We feel that he will be working with us.”

Chelsea ended the Australian leg of their tour with a late 2-1 defeat to London rivals Tottenham, who had ten men for almost the entire second half.

The Blues were without goalkeeper Robert Sanchez, who suffered a small knock.



Meanwhile, striker Joao Pedro is in talks over a new contract with the club, who are confident he will agree terms.

Pedro was a target for Barcelona at the start of the summer window, but Chelsea dubbed the Brazilian striker “untouchable” this summer and are pushing to tie him down further.

The forward only joined from Brighton last summer and the 24-year-old’s deal currently runs until 2033.

Sports.title: It’s a nice surprise to discover deep down football has a backbone.. but where’s this show of strength been hiding?
Sports.content:
WHAT a pleasant surprise to discover that­, buried deep, football actually does have a backbone.

It has been a delight to watch the sordid plan of suit-and-trainer wearing — creepy uncle at a wedding style — Gianni Infantino ­collapse around his own not-insignificant ears.



Uefa’s threat to boycott all but started the snowball.

Others attempted to look brave as they scrambled aboard the bandwagon which had been impressively assembled by Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin.



But, sorry to complain at what is undoubtedly a triumph in the face of attempts to ­further b*****dise football, where has this sudden show of strength been when we needed it before?

Football has needed this newly-discovered might of its leaders and governing bodies time and time again.

Yet they have often been too cowardly or self-interested to stand up for supporters or those they represent.

Where were you when we needed to stop hydration breaks, half-time shows, Sunday night kick-offs or the omnipresence of that ‘Here we go’ touting wally on social media? It is true they are trivial points but all of them have got under the skin of fans at one point or another in recent years.

They are also a window to the serious problems which occur across the game, and all too often involve Fifa.

Belgium, Germany and Norway all publicly expressed their dismay over Fifa’s bowing to Donald Trump over Folarin Balogun’s one-match suspension for the United States’ round of 16 tie at the World Cup.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The decision to allow the striker to face Belgium was as dodgy as they come and they did not even try to hide that fact from us all.

As soon as the world learned that Infantino had taken calls from the US President — who just happened to have been the recipient of the first Fifa Peace Prize — a boycott would have been fitting.

It may seem extreme but Infantino’s spineless approach to Trump tainted his precious tournament.

What was the point of everyone else ­putting all that effort in if the hosts could fix any problems with a phone call to the man who is supposed to uphold and champion the rules?



Even though Belgium dismantled a Balogun-led USA 4-1 in the last-16, a united front at that moment — in the middle of a major tournament — would have made quite the statement, one Infantino and Fifa could not have stood up to.

Ticket prices, the barring of Sudanese referee Omar Artan from officiating at the tournament and the treatment of Iran were all largely greeted with a shrug from around the world.

Uefa quickly sailed in to appoint Artan to their Super Cup match between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa this month.

But that appeared to stem from a dislike of Infantino and a shot at a quick PR win rather than anything more moral.



A firm stance in Qatar at the World Cup four years ago would have been welcomed.

Instead the European nations’ show of support for human rights and the LGBTQ+ community fell down under the ­terrifying threat of a yellow card.

Those Fifa-approved armbands Harry Kane and his fellow captains ended up sporting in 2022 must have really warmed the hearts of the oppressed in the Middle East.

None of this is to say that Ceferin has not done well to gather the whole of Europe into what is undoubtedly a noble stand.



It would have been easy to swing the powerful nations behind a boycott but smaller federations tempted by Infantino’s promise of riches would have taken persuading.

This must set the tone for what Uefa has to stand for going forwards if it is to mean anything.

Let’s not forget this is a body which bowed to the Super League plotters by needlessly expanding the Champions League, dulling the experience for fans and piling more minutes into the legs of shattered stars.

Wake-up calls for those at the top are always helpful but did the collapse of the Super League really prevent Europe’s powerhouses from running the game? No.

Governing bodies must fight for football more often, otherwise their standing up to Fifa merely looks to be a move laced in self-interest by Uefa’s top man.



ED’S TOON’S BEST BET

A PAL in the pub recently lumped a few quid on Newcastle to get relegated at 40-1.

The fact he is a Sunderland fan may have tipped the scales but it is looking like a spot of superb foresight.

Just over a week on and that price has collapsed and may shorten further after the Toon effectively forced out their greatest asset in recent years.

Up against the expectations of a club the size of Newcastle, let alone their Saudi benefactors, Eddie Howe overdelivered given what he had to work with.

Chronic mismanagement and snail-paced decision-making made it an impossible task and, for his sake, it was wise to jump now.



Should his next club offer proper support, they will be very lucky indeed — as I would be if I listened to my mate’s tips more often.

RISEN FROM THE ASHES

THE drumbeat for Ben Stokes’ Ashes return appears to have started a little over a month after he retired.

All England fans want to see him in one last dust-up with the Aussies.

And given the narcissistic way he left the international stage, they may well get their wish — albeit not as captain.



Stokes will not be able to resist the storyline of riding back into the Test side next year to beat Australia.

FANS IN A MUD-DLE

CONFIRMATION that he is allowed to start playing football again will have been a delight to Mykhailo Mudryk after his doping ban.

The news was celebrated by some Chelsea supporters as if the Ukrainian would return like a new mega-money signing, a fresh star for Xabi Alonso to work with.

Have they forgotten just how hopeless the winger was at times?

Ten goals in 73 appearances does not scream superstar.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

I watched him play ten minutes of a charity match at Stamford Bridge — and he even struggled in that.

Those fans may soon recall why they were not too bothered by his suspension in the first place.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino's ill-fated scheming does not mean a 64-team World Cup should be written off
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino's ill-fated scheming does not mean a 64-team World Cup should be written off

FIFA president Gianni Infantino is somehow still clinging to his job but a consultation process is still taking place over the possible expansion of the World Cup in 2030

View 4 Images Cape Verde and their goalkeeper Vozinha captured the imagination of football fans around the world (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The news - the predictable news - that FIFA has already begun a consultation process ahead of making a decision about expanding the World Cup to include 64 teams was met not only with widespread incredulity but with utter cynicism.

‌



And there was one of the many fundamental problems with Gianni Infantino’s heinous, thankfully ill-fated scheme to sell off a chunk of the World Cup to billionaire cronies.

‌



It meant everything suggested by FIFA will feel rotten. This expansion idea was immediately seen, certainly in Europe, as just another ruse to make more money for FIFA and for the private investors that Infantino wanted to ingratiate himself with - and make fortunes from. No-one could have been blamed for looking at it from that point of view.

‌



UEFA declare loss of confidence in Gianni Infantino in bombshell new statement READ MORE :

The secret of comedy is timing, but there was nothing funny about FIFA saying they are, essentially, rushing through their consultation period - a decision will be made as soon as August 14 - just a couple of days after Infantino’s plot to raise $20billion by auctioning off rights packages to the World Cup was revealed. Bigger World Cup, more money for those private investor mates that, mercifully, will now not be directly involved in the tournament.

No wonder the news that the prospect of a 64-team World Cup is being accelerated by FIFA fat-cats was met with almost complete scorn. That is where power-crazed, money-obsessed Infantino has taken FIFA.

Yet would a 64-team World Cup be that bad? If the extra revenue was not going to private investors - and that prospect has been summarily headed off by UEFA’s threat of a boycott - would a 64-team World Cup be one of FIFA’s worst offences? No.

‌



View 4 Images Curacao were another small nation to make their mark on World Cup 2026 (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Hands up, I was against the tournament being expanded to 48 from 32 teams but was soon converted once Cape Verde started doing their stuff. I was converted when Curacao equalised against Germany, even though they were hammered 7-1.

I was converted by the entertainment provided by the group stages. I was converted by the joy of every nation’s set of fans.

‌



The only downside I could find was that the third games in the group stages were open to contrivance. That is because whittling 48 teams down to 32 for the knockout stages involves having eight third-placed finishers as qualifiers.

As it happened, there was no evidence of contrivance, but quite simply, 64 into 32 goes better. Sixteen groups of four, top two in each group qualify. Easy.

View 4 Images Gianni Infantino is under increasing pressure to stand down as FIFA president (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

‌



The next World Cup in 2030 - the centenary edition - is being staged in Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay hosting opening-round matches. There will be enough venues to accommodate 64 teams.

As UEFA and its president Aleksander Ceferin are now at permanent odds with FIFA and Infantino, they might not like the idea of an expansion to 64 teams. They will probably oppose it.

Yet the Euros is a 24-team competition, meaning 43.63 per cent of its member nations qualify for the finals. A 64-team World Cup would mean 30.34 per cent of FIFA member nations would qualify.

‌



View 4 Images Spain lifted the World Cup trophy at the end of a 48-team tournament that was widely deemed a success (Image: David Ramos/Getty Images)

Those of us who were originally in the camp that thought the World Cup should be for the elite only have long lost the argument. It turns out it was not a bad one to lose. Did you begrudge any of the teams at the 2026 World Cup their time in the sun?

And now it is a 48-team tournament - there will be no consultation process about any possible reduction in competitors - what is an extra 16 teams between friends? Italy might even qualify.

Article continues below

Understandably, an expansion would be negatively linked with Infantino’s scheming. But he will be long gone by then, surely. And the 64 teams who compete at the 2030 World Cup can enjoy themselves, untainted by his presidency and private ownership.

Sports.title: Liverpool have been given green light for 'dream' Bradley Barcola alternative
Sports.content:
Liverpool have been given green light for 'dream' Bradley Barcola alternative

Liverpool are in the market for a Mohamed Salah replacement for the new Premier League season

View 2 Images Liverpool want to sign Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty)

Liverpool are stepping up their efforts to sign Bradley Barcola from PSG. But there are other potential options out there if a move fails to materialise, notably AFC Bournemouth's Brazilian sensation, Rayan.

‌



The Reds are preparing an opening bid for Barcola, who is understood to be keen on a move to Anfield. However, the Frenchman's price tag could prove a sticking point.

‌



Barcola is valued by the Ligue 1 champions at £145million. Not only would that represent a Premier League record transfer, it is also some way above the £100m mark that Liverpool chiefs would prefer to do business at.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Should the winger's price prove insurmountable in negotiations, the Reds could turn their attention to Rayan instead. The 19-year-old has been linked with a host of clubs, including the Liverpool, after impressing for Bournemouth following his January move to the south coast.

‌



Indeed, talkSPORT reports that the Bournemouth star is considered a 'dream' target for the Reds. However, the teenager's release clause of £85m will not kick in until 2027, meaning that Andoni Iraola may need to fork out more for his signature in the short term.

One person who is very aware of Rayan's abilities is Cherries midfielder, Marcus Tavernier. The 27-year-old showered his team-mate with praise following Bournemouth's 3-0 win over Crystal Palace in May, even going so far as to predict that his stay at the Vitality Stadium would be short lived given his exceptional talents.

View 2 Images Rayan could prove a good alternative to Barcola (Image: Getty)

‌



He told Sky Sports: "Rayan and Kroupi? It’s been unbelievable, they are two world-class talents. I don’t think they will be at Bournemouth for a long period of time give the quality they have got.

"It’s brilliant to have them on the pitch. As a team we give the young players the confidence to go out and play with freedom."

Barcola is evidently still Liverpool's main target, with the Reds expected to submit an offer imminently. But with the sums involved in securing a deal, there's no guarantee a move will happen - and that could lead Iraola to look elsewhere.

Article continues below

PSG argue that the France international is now a back-to-back Champions League winner and should be priced above the likes of Morgan Rogers - who went to Chelsea for £117m - and City's £116m move for Elliot Anderson.

It is understood that Barcola is not planning to sign a new deal in France and has just two years remaining on his current contract.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola’s three new Liverpool starting XIs with blockbuster Bradley Barcola transfer
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola’s three new Liverpool starting XIs with blockbuster Bradley Barcola transfer

Liverpool could line up in a number of interesting ways under Andoni Iraola

View 4 Images Bradley Barcola is a major target for Liverpool (Image: Anne-Christine POUJOULAT / AFP via Getty Images)

Liverpool have been relatively quiet in the transfer market compared to 12 months ago – so far. The Reds dropped a whopping £446million on the likes of Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike, Florian Wirtz and Milos Kerkez ahead of the 2024-25 Premier League season.

‌



But that outlay didn't result in the retention of the title as Arne Slot's side ended up trophyless and the Dutchman out of a job. Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate followed the Dutchman out the door following the expiry of their respective contracts.

‌



Now, a new era is set to begin under Andoni Iraola. The former Bournemouth boss has signed Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz so far, but fans would argue that they will need more reinforcements before the season begins.

‌



One major target Iraola is focusing on is Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola. The winger is not an out-and-out replacement for Salah, but he can slot into multiple areas if Liverpool does complete his signing.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



The Reds face Newcastle in just three weeks' time and also have a number of players sidelined for this curtain raiser. Conor Bradley, Joe Gomez, Ekitike and Giovanni Leoni are all unavailable, meaning Iraola will need to adapt.

Should Barcola be brought in before the Premier League opener, and Munoz also available, the Reds could set up totally differently going forward. Here, Mirror Football details three ways Liverpool could line up if the PSG star does join.

4-2-3-1

View 4 Images This is Iraola's trusted system (Image: Supplied)

‌



Iraola will probably opt to implement his trusted system from his Bournemouth tenure with Alisson Becker anticipated to stay as No. 1 this season.

This setup would allow the Reds to operate a flat back four with active wing-backs in Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong, alongside Virgil van Dijk and Jacquet at centre-back.

It's in midfield where a double pivot of Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch could anchor the side, while a lethal attacking trio of Rio Ngumoha, Wirtz and Barcola would operate behind Isak leading the line.

‌



In this setup, Barcola would occupy his preferred left-sided position, where he has netted 32 goals and provided 32 assists for PSG and Lyon. Ngumoha would play on the right, a switch Iraola deployed in the recent pre-season victory over Wrexham, while Wirtz would orchestrate play in his natural No. 10 role.

4-3-3

View 4 Images This formation could be played around with by the boss (Image: Supplied)

With the same goalkeeper and defensive quartet, the alteration here arrives in midfield. Szoboszlai, Gravenberch and Wirtz would create a more conventional engine room, with the German playmaker granted licence to drift while the Dutchman operates in a deeper position.

‌



It's in attack where Iraola could tinker, too. Barcola could operate on the right, a flank the Frenchman isn't completely accustomed to, but does possess experience in.

The PSG man has just seven goals from the right but has contributed 15 assists. New signing Munoz would slot into his preferred position on the left flank with both wide men delivering balls into Isak, who would operate as a lone striker.

This could even shift into a compact 4-5-1 without possession, should the Reds need to protect a lead.

‌



4-4-1-1

View 4 Images This formation could bring some chaos for the Reds (Image: Supplied)

This setup places Wirtz on the left and Ngumoha on the right of a four-man midfield, with Szoboszlai and Gravenberch forming a two-man defensive shield. However, this would represent Iraola's wildcard option, potentially shifting Barcola into the hole behind Isak.

Barcola has featured as a centre-forward on more than 20 occasions, contributing a respectable nine goals. It's not an extensive sample, but the winger is known for cutting inside and frequently taking on opponents in central areas.

Article continues below

With a dependable midfield quartet behind him, and Wirtz and Ngumoha controlling the supply lines down either flank, Barcola could be handed the opportunity to forge a lethal partnership with Isak, operating just behind him in an unfamiliar yet potentially devastating No. 10 role.

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson convinced Arsenal fan to snub Gunners for Man Utd in transfer U-turn
Sports.content:
Sir Alex Ferguson convinced Arsenal fan to snub Gunners for Man Utd in transfer U-turn

Manchester United have battled with plenty of Premier League sides for transfers over the years

View 2 Images Chris Smalling joined Manchester United after speaking with Sir Alex Ferguson (Image: Matthew Peters/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Sir Alex Ferguson convinced Chris Smalling to abandon his dream to play for Arsenal and join Manchester United instead. The defender grew up a fan of the Gunners and was sure he would join his beloved club from Fulham.

‌



The north London outfit were in talks with the Cottagers as Arsene Wenger's reputation for developing rising stars interested Smalling. However, Sir Alex jumped in with a pitch that the centre-half just couldn't turn down.

‌



He told The Athletic: "In my head, I was going to Arsenal. Then Manchester United got in touch. I was leaving the team bus at Blackburn away and [Fulham boss] Roy Hodgson said, 'We’ve accepted a bid from Man United.' That threw me.

‌



"I felt there were more opportunities to play at Arsenal, but I spoke to Fergie and he said, 'I wouldn’t sign you if I didn’t think you could play games.' Maybe his aura felt right, but I made the right decision because I was soon playing alongside great players and winning the league."

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd get fresh Benjamin Sesko injury update after star missed pre-season friendlies READ MORE :

Fergie's words stuck with Smalling and he joined United for an initial fee of around £8million, which rose to £12m due to appearance and performance bonuses. This was a major success story for a defender who had been playing non-league football just two years before his move to Old Trafford.

‌



Smalling had been at Maidstone in 2008 and ended up at Fulham, who were paying him just £5,000-a-week. He quadrupled his salary by joining United but his former non-league side didn't receive a penny, as he was a non-contract player when he departed the Stones.

Arsenal had met Fulham's clause of £10m before United swooped in, but Sir Alex's words alone convinced Smalling to ignore the allure of Wenger and head to Manchester instead. The Arsenal snub proved a wise decision for Smalling, as he would go on to win two Premier League titles and the Europa League with United.

View 2 Images Sir Alex Ferguson's 'aura' had Smalling convinced (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

‌



The defender also won numerous domestic cups and came runner-up in the Champions League final in his first year at Old Trafford. Smalling made 323 appearances for United over a decade, scoring 18 goals and assisting three times.

He joined Roma on loan for the 2019/20 season and became the first English player to score at least two goals in the same Serie A campaign since fellow United alumni David Beckham.

The centre-half joined the Italian outfit permanently for a fee of £17m and spent four years there before moving on to Al-Fayha. Smalling is now 36 years old and without a club, though he hasn't announced plans of retirement yet.

Sports.title: Man Utd’s dream final month of transfer window: £85m midfielder joins and three deals done
Sports.content:
Man Utd’s dream final month of transfer window: £85m midfielder joins and three deals done

Manchester United could make multiple dream signings before transfer deadline day on September 1

View 3 Images Michael Carrick will likely be busy in August (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have secured several new signings but Michael Carrick's team remain busy in the transfer market. As August arrives, the club have one month remaining to restructure their squad.

‌



The middle of the park remains a priority, despite signing Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. United have been linked with numerous possibilities but the manager may seek to deliver a marquee name in midfield to underline the club's aspirations to challenge for major honours next season.

‌



In attack, Benjamin Sesko requires competition, with striker Joshua Zirkzee among several players who could depart Old Trafford this summer. Meanwhile, United could begin long-term planning by testing Newcastle's determination over left-back Lewis Hall. Here, Mirror Football examines what a dream end to the transfer window might look like for the club.

‌



£85m midfielder signs

Aurelien Tchouameni arriving from Real Madrid would mark a statement signing for United in the final weeks of the window. The Red Devils refused to pay astronomical sums for the likes of Elliot Anderson, Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes earlier in the summer but splashing out on Tchouameni would emphasise the club's ambitions.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The 26-year-old would represent an ideal signing for Carrick's revamped midfield as the United manager reshapes his squad following Casemiro's departure. Spanish publication AS previously reported that Real Madrid would seek around £85m for Tchouameni after the France international recently penned a contract extension with Los Blancos.

‌



Man Utd open to offers for four more players as Michael Carrick wields transfer axe READ MORE :

However, the Spanish heavyweights are keen on Manchester City's Rodri, which could prompt Tchouameni to weigh up his options elsewhere. It would provide Carrick with an impressive selection of midfielders, with Tielemans, Santos and Kobbie Mainoo all competing for spots in the United starting XI.

Lewis Hall deal

United are interested in Newcastle left-back Lewis Hall and, in an ideal scenario, would secure Luke Shaw's long-term replacement this summer. The 21-year-old has caught the eye during his spell with the Magpies, who have already demonstrated a readiness to offload key assets through the departures of Anthony Gordon and Tonali.

The England international is reportedly open to joining Carrick's side. Yet Newcastle are believed to be hesitant about selling another prized asset, meaning United may need to fork out a substantial fee for the defender, who left Chelsea for £35m in 2023.

‌



View 3 Images Lewis Hall is reportedly open to joining Manchester United (Image: Michael Driver/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

United depended heavily on Shaw throughout last season but will have worries about the seasoned full-back staying injury-free, while Patrick Dorgu appeared more effective when deployed on the left wing. Completing a move for Hall would enable United to begin their left-back succession planning early, even if the young defender commands a substantial transfer fee.

New striker joins

Benjamin Sesko's unavailability for United's early pre-season fixtures has underlined the club's need to add a striker before the summer window closes. Joshua Zirkzee has spearheaded the attack for Carrick's team but has struggled to establish himself since his arrival from Bologna in 2024, prompting reports of a possible £30m return to Serie A.

‌



While Sesko flourished after Carrick arrived at United, it took time for the Slovenian forward to cement his place in the starting lineup. The 23-year-old is still developing and shouldn't be the club's sole senior striker as United prepare for a Champions League campaign and seek to improve upon their third-place Premier League finish.

View 3 Images Dusan Vlahovic is a free agent after leaving Juventus (Image: Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images)

Dusan Vlahovic is among several forwards to be linked with a move to Old Trafford and could offer the perfect answer to United's dilemma. The 26-year-old is a free agent after leaving Juventus this summer, where he netted 68 goals across 168 matches.

Article continues below

An expensive, high-profile signing could potentially hinder Sesko's development under Carrick and stop him from fulfilling his true potential. However, the former RB Leipzig star would benefit from competing alongside Vlahovic, who would equally be afforded the chance to impress as a rotation option at Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Fresh Bradley Barcola transfer boost as improved bid to go in for star
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Fresh Bradley Barcola transfer boost as improved bid to go in for star

Liverpool round-up as Bradley Barcola negotiations take a turn in the Reds' favour

View 3 Images Liverpool's interest in Bradley Barcola remains strong (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool's transfer window has been quieter than many fans had hoped so far. But it may be about to stir into life as negotiations with Paris Saint-Germain over long-running target Bradley Barcola continue.

‌



Pre-season has been promising with wins over Sunderland and Wrexham. Next up on the tour of the United States is a meeting with Leeds United at Chicago's Soldier Field.

‌



New signings Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz are yet to figure. The former is getting closer to his Reds debut following a shoulder injury, while Spain World Cup winner Munoz is coming to the end of his post-tournament break.

‌



It's the interest in Barcola that continues to take centre stage, with movement elsewhere in the transfer market strengthening the Reds' hand. Here's a round-up of the latest Liverpool transfer news.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Barcola replacements found

PSG are close to landing two wingers in a clear sign they are preparing for life after Barcola. They have reportedly opened talks with Ajax about signing Mika Godts for £51million.

‌



Yan Diomande transfer twist as surprise update emerges on Real Madrid target READ MORE :

Liverpool news: Green light given for huge transfer offer as talks for new signing begin READ MORE :

Meanwhile, the Champions League holders are on the verge of signing Maghnes Akliouche from Monaco for around £43m. With Desire Doue, Ibrahim Maye and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia already at the club, the position is set to become even more crowded.

Something needs to give, and that 'something' is Barcola. Liverpool have no intention of meeting PSG's £145m asking price but negotiations are continuing and the impending arrival of Godts and Akliouche should strengthen their hand.

The French champions still stand to make an enormous profit on a player who arrived from Lyon for less than £40m three years ago.

‌



View 3 Images Bradley Barcola's PSG exit has moved closer (Image: Anne-Christine POUJOULAT / AFP via Getty Images)

New Jones offer

Inter Milan are willing to increase their offer for midfielder Curtis Jones. The Serie A champions have already brought John Stones to the club this summer and are keen to add another England international, having already had one bid of around £21m rejected.

As reported by the Liverpool Echo, Inter are preparing a bid of £30m, although that is still short of the Reds' £35m valuation for the 25-year-old, who has a year left on his contract.

‌



View 3 Images Curtis Jones is attracting interest (Image: 2026 Liverpool FC)

Intermediaries working on behalf of Inter have now contacted Liverpool once more and have informed them of the Serie A side's willingness to up their offer. Jones has made 228 appearances since his debut in January 2019 but has struggled for regular first-team football.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Transfer 'approved' as £70m target 'open' to Old Trafford switch
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Transfer 'approved' as £70m target 'open' to Old Trafford switch

It's been a busy summer for Manchester United - and their transfer business looks far from over, with a number of targets still on their radar

View 3 Images Michael Carrick is looking to make a few more signings this summer (Image: Getty)

Manchester United have wasted little time getting to work this summer - but their rebuild is far from complete. With the 2026/27 campaign fast approaching, the priority is to maintain the momentum generated at the end of last season and ensure Michael Carrick's side are equipped to hit the ground running.

‌



Having spent the previous two summer windows addressing issues in attack and defence, the focus has now shifted towards strengthening the midfield. United have already made significant moves in that department, with Andrey Santos arriving from Chelsea in a £50million deal and Youri Tielemans joining from Aston Villa for £35m.

‌



However, the business is not expected to stop there. The club remain active in the market and continue to monitor a number of high-profile targets, including reinforcements beyond midfield as they look to complete a much-needed squad overhaul.

‌



With plenty still to unfold before the window closes, here are the latest Manchester United transfer headlines.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Marcus Rashford has chance to 'hurt' Man Utd as two transfer moves proposed READ MORE :

Man Utd 'internally approve' Hall transfer

Lewis Hall has emerged as a top target for United this summer, with reports claiming an official approach for the Newcastle defender has been approved internally. The England international has been linked with a move away from St James' Park for some time, with United among a number of Premier League heavyweights keeping a close eye on his situation.

‌



The Red Devils see Hall as a potential long-term replacement for Luke Shaw and are reportedly considering an opening bid worth around £60m for the 21-year-old. Although Hall remains tied down to Newcastle until 2029, the significant upheaval at the club could potentially open the door to an exit.

View 3 Images Lewis Hall is high on Man United's wish list (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

The Magpies have already seen Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe all leave in recent weeks, while Bruno Guimaraes is expected to follow suit in the coming days. Hall could yet follow them through the exit door, although Newcastle's impressive summer sales could actually strengthen their negotiating position.

‌



Having already generated around £170m through player departures - a figure that could rise towards £250m if Guimaraes completes his proposed switch to Arsenal - Newcastle are under no financial pressure to cash in on Hall.

Scott 'open to Man Utd move'

Manchester United could be set to make their third major midfield signing of the summer, with Bournemouth star Alex Scott reportedly open to the possibility of joining Carrick's side. The 22-year-old is attracting significant interest from across the Premier League, with Liverpool, Chelsea and Arsenal also keeping tabs on his situation.

View 3 Images Bournemouth's Alex Scott is reportedly open to a move to Manchester United (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

‌



Scott is believed to be considering all options at this stage, with no clear frontrunner emerging in the race for his signature. Reports claim Chelsea recently saw a £64m offer rejected by Bournemouth, although that does not necessarily put them ahead of their rivals in what remains a fiercely contested transfer battle.

The Cherries are thought to value Scott at around £70m, but given the level of competition for his services, that asking price could climb closer to £80m. United would then need to weigh up whether such a sizeable outlay represents good value.

The Red Devils remain keen to add another central midfielder after their pursuit of Atalanta star Ederson collapsed, but their recent recruitment strategy has typically focused on more measured, cost-effective deals rather than marquee spending.
