Australia coach Andrew McDonald completed his coaching badges by the age of 27, cutting his teeth here seven years later, starting at the bottom of the pile with a Leicestershire side that had gone winless for two seasons while continue to play back in his homeland.

In improving the midlands club’s finishing positions in both the 2015 and 2016 seasons, he established a reputation as one of the brightest young coaches on the global circuit, something he gave further credence to when in his first senior coaching position in Australia he marked his debut campaign of 2016-17 by taking Victoria to the Sheffield Shield title.

At Grace Road, McDonald could put into play his belief in a hands-off approach, making players take greater responsibility and use his own previous struggles with the mental side of the sport to liberate the thinking of a team previously suffocated by struggle.

The fierce loyalty he has developed towards players was arguably forged through witnessing a group of low achievers rise above their stations with the right backing.

The art of managing people, he says, is what he invested in most as a coach. A six-month season that barely pauses for breath allows the time to get to know the individuals concerned. It gave him a steep learning curve.

Ottis Gibson won the Twenty20 World Cup with West Indies, defeated both Australia and India in Test series while in charge of South Africa and was England’s bowling coach on two occasions, having gone through the ECB coaching programme in the first decade of this century.

Gibson was mentored by an Australian Troy Cooley, but both were very much part of the English system.

Another Australian Jason Gillespie was exposed to the pressure of ending Yorkshire’s trophy drought as a young coach fresh from a maiden stint in Zimbabwe, and responded by delivering back-to-back Championships in 2014-15. Like Gibson, he moved onto the international scene, albeit briefly, with Pakistan.

Others are grateful for what the county system offers. Perhaps it’s time for us to be so too.

Sports.title: Club at centre of 'Clicky Ponting' scandal hit by fresh 'cheating' claims as umpire releases footage of ANOTHER player seemingly clicking fingers
Sports.content:
A fresh controversy has engulfed the amateur cricket club at the centre of the 'Clicky Ponting' cheating scandal after an umpire released footage appearing to show another player deploying the same tactic.

Saltburn Cricket Club has been at the centre of a storm after fielder Brian Devine allegedly cheated during a Second XI Division Two match against Norton. Video footage of Devine appearing to be clicking his fingers to mimic the sound of a bat edge, tricking the umpire into giving the batsman out, went viral on social media.

On Monday, the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League launched an investigation into Devine, 38, who has since been suspended by the club for the 'foreseeable future'.

Now, fresh footage has emerged appearing to show another Saltburn player successfully using the same tactic during a Third XI match against Marton.

The fielder appears to click his fingers as the ball flies past the bat and into the wicketkeeper's gloves, prompting the on-field umpire to give the batsman out. The footage was posted on social media by Berkshire-based umpire Andy Smy.

The captain of another team in the same league earlier this week claimed the alleged tactic had not been confined to Saltburn's victory over Norton.

Saltburn have been widely condemned on social media following multiple videos emerging

He said: 'It was not confined to just one game. I was at the other end when one of our players was dismissed and I heard a big sound as the ball went through and immediately thought: "He's out."

'The umpire didn't hesitate either, but our batsman was adamant he was nowhere near the ball and couldn't understand the loud click.

'In all we had three batsmen given out caught behind, but all of them said they hadn't touched the ball. One protested so much the umpire had to speak to him and threaten him with a warning.

'I know of at least three other teams who now have suspicions and it should be noted that in one match against Shildon their wicketkeeper took eight catches.

'You hear of all kinds of things going on in cricket but this is something I haven't heard of before. I hope the league takes appropriate action.'

Earlier this week, Saltburn's Second XI forfeited their match against Marton, dumping themselves out of a cup competition, with a source close to the league saying 'none of the players will have wanted anything to do with this game while they're under such focus'.

They did, however, return to the field on Saturday for a league match against Marton, where table-toppers Saltburn crashed to a nine-wicket defeat. With Devine no longer fielding at slip, Marton chased down their target of 101 in just 20 overs.

Amateur cricket player Brian Devine has been caught appearing to click his fingers to make it appear that a batter has been caught behind when in fact they haven't hit the ball at all

Devine has been dubbed as 'Clicky Ponting' on social media for his alleged actions on the cricket field

Saltburn player has been caught on camera seeming to be clicking his fingers

And Devine, a father and auction mart worker from Guisborough, North Yorkshire, is planning to 'lie low' until the scandal dies down.

A friend said: 'Brian is completely bewildered by the way this has gone all around the world.

'He's had an Australian podcast offering to pay his legal bills today - it's the first he's heard that he's got any legal bills and he's hoping it won't get that far.

'His mates have been telling him to sell his story in Australia, but he just wants it all to go away and hopes he can get back to playing cricket, though at the moment that feels impossible.

'He woke up on Monday morning thinking the world was still the same place he'd left it the night before and suddenly his story was all over the world - in Australia, India, New Zealand and the UK, of course.

'He understands why there is an investigation but the reaction from around the world has knocked him sideways.'

The North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League said it was treating the allegations of cheating 'with the utmost seriousness' and called for the 'rights of all parties' to be respected amid intense scrutiny on social media.

'We would want to place on record our genuine concern for the welfare of those at Saltburn Cricket Club and ask for all to take that into account. There are many people at the club and one of our aims will be to provide them with any wellbeing support we can,' the league said.

'Whilst we understand, to some degree, the interest this issue has generated in the press and media, it is imperative that, now this process is under way, the rights of all parties are observed, including the overriding principles of natural justice and the right to a fair hearing for any individual or entity concerned.

'Anything less risks prejudicing any formal action which may follow.'

Saltburn, in a statement on Wednesday, said: 'This has been a very distressing and stressful experience for all those concerned, and we would ask that this reality is borne in mind and that personal boundaries are respected, as we are an amateur club run entirely by volunteers.'

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta insists Arsenal will be 'very ambitious' in the transfer market with club refusing to give up on sensational Vinicius Jr deal
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta would not be drawn on questions about Arsenal's interest in Vinicius Junior, but he did insist the champions were ‘very ambitious’ and ‘won’t sit still’ in the summer market.

The 26-year-old winger has been heavily linked with a move to north London as Arteta looks to bolster his frontline.

Vinicius’ contract at Real Madrid expires next summer and the Gunners are interested in signing the player.

Just days after Arteta said that new signings are needed to take Arsenal to a ‘different dimension’, he doubled down on his assertions.

When asked about whether more signings are expected in light of the Vinicius reports, Arteta said following Arsenal’s 4-1 pre-season victory over Girona: ‘Well we are really active, trying to improve and evolve the team. That's clear.

‘We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else.

Vinicius’ contract at Real Madrid expires next summer and the Gunners are interested in signing the 26-year-old Brazilian winger

‘And you can just see it. The transfer market and our opponents, what we are doing - we won't sit still. And we are very ambitious in what we want to do.

‘The margins are very small. And because we want to get better and the level is going to increase, we need to increase the competition internally. We need to make sure we identify the things that we don't have in the team, to have bigger margins. And that's the way we have to think.’

Max Dowman shone with a goal and an assist in the match, issuing a reminder ahead of what could be an important season for the 16-year-old.

‘That's what we want,’ added Arteta. 'When you play for Arsenal, the expectations should be high and should be expecting really good things.

'We know what he's (Dowman) capable of doing. We want to be more consistent in terms of the performances and the actions that he can deliver.

‘But I think today he had a really good game.’

Sports.title: Dominant Josh Kerr powers to gold in the mile race at Commonwealth Games - two weeks after shattering world record
Sports.content:
Dominant Josh Kerr powers to gold in the mile race at Commonwealth Games - two weeks after shattering world record

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It felt like the ghosts of 1954 were chasing Josh Kerr down the home straight of the Scotstoun track. Stories from the famous battle between Sir Roger Bannister and John Landy pumped nostalgia into every step of this Miracle Mile.

Queen Elizabeth II was just two years into her reign for that epic clash in Vancouver. Her great grandchildren were in the crowd for this one, braving the Glaswegian chill to watch Kerr push and shove his way to gold.

More than seven decades have passed since Bannister's victory but Kerr's spirit when he made his move in the final lap would survive the test of time. The Scotsman was boxed in with 400 metres to go, before he shoved Kenya's Brian Komen out of the way and charged from the middle of the pack.

This is the place where Kerr set personal bests in the shot put and high jump as a schoolboy. He watched his brother play rugby here for Edinburgh and, at times, this race had the physicality of a Scottish scrum.

'Welcome the world champion and the world record holder,' blasted the stadium announcer. As if this race did not have enough storylines to it, the stadium announcer was the father of fellow Scot Jake Wightman, who finished sixth.

Like Kerr, Wightman knows this place well. Both raced here for Edinburgh Athletics Club as juniors. Wightman is renowned for his sprint finish but he could not catch Kerr, who turned his bedroom into an altitude chamber to increase his lung capacity for moments like this.

Scotland's Josh Kerr surged clear of the field to claim a dominant gold medal in the mile event

There was even more anticipation for this race than when Usain Bolt stepped onto the Glasgow track for the relay in 2014. Hometown heroes, champions, record holders, Olympians were all in the mix. This was a world-class field.

Two weeks ago, Kerr broke the mile record at London Stadium. Bannister and Landy did the same before Vancouver, famously breaching the four-minute barrier for the first time.

They did not have the same footwear as the Scotsman, whose running spikes were engineered in a laboratory in Seattle.

'It definitely felt a little bit overkill - like driving a formula one car along the street for a cup of coffee,' said Kerr after his heat on Thursday.

To the untrained eye, they look like trainers that are missing the heel. Their 'rocking' midsole is designed to maximise the energy return on every stride. They were formulated to break the world record at London Stadium, where Kerr had smooth pacemakers and the shelter of ginormous stands.

Championship racing is different. The racers constantly changed pace as they jostled for position - with Botswana's Thesipo Masalela setting the pace in the opening lap.

Gusts of wind rip through Scotstoun, whipping up the 74 Commonwealth flags behind the finish line. The heatwave in the south of England, it is safe to say, did not make its way to Glasgow.

Kerr's face has greeted every commuter arriving into Glasgow, his image looming large on the billboards outside Central Station. He slicked back his hair before the starting gun, having had a fresh trim a few hours before the race. He knew this was his moment to shine.

'This is absolutely incredible,' he said. 'Doing it in front of the Scottish crowd where I learned how to race. I came here week after week as a kid. I didn't waste any energy. I knew the opportunity would open up and I had enough energy to put a gap on them in the last few hundred. I went early to save everyone some stress.

'With the World Indoors and going after the record in London, this was the one we had circled on the calendar before any of that.

'I didn't put together my performance I wanted in Birmingham 2022. I think a British crowd deserved more from me – I owed them that for sure.

No Scotsman has been named BBC Sports Personality of the Year since Andy Murray in 2016. The bookies had Kerr as joint favourite with Jude Bellingham to be named sports personality of the year before this race. This victory may well nudge the odds in his favour.

Interest in middle distance racing has waned over the years. Seb Coe, Steve Ovett, and Steve Cram enjoyed a golden era in the 1980s. This race felt like a resurrection.

Sports.title: Former Man City captain, 56, gives positive health update after being diagnosed with devastating neurological condition as he returns to co-commentary work
Sports.content:
Former Manchester City captain Andy Morrison has given an encouraging update on his health following his battle with devastating neurological condition Ramsay Hunt Syndrome.

Morrison, 56, revealed in a heartbreaking video online earlier this year that he was battling the condition as he vowed to fight the disorder.

In May, he appeared in good spirits as he explained his symptoms and detailed how his recovery was going to take 'a long, long time'.

Now, however, in a new video, Morrison appeared to be much further down his road to recovery as he revealed he has returned to commentary work.

'Evening everyone,' he began after work covering City's pre-season defeat by Inter Milan. 'Just a quick update after the first day back working at City with the matchday live team, which I thoroughly enjoyed.

'It was fantastic to be back. Felt the voice was strong enough to go back and do co-commentary today. That's my first time back in five-and-a-half months. I really appreciate all the support and working with Ali Mann, who makes it very easy.

Great to be back 🩵⚽️🙏 pic.twitter.com/VW1nUplE0N — Andy Morrison (@AndyMorri5on) August 1, 2026

Former Manchester City captain Andy Morrison has given fans an update on his battle with a devastating neurological condition. Left: pictured this week, right: pictured in May

The former defender previously revealed that it will take him a year to fully recover

'An enjoyable game. I struggled with a few words, a few names, but nothing too bad. I did struggle with (Ryan) McAidoo. Could have a player there by the way, watch this space. There was enough there to think he could be the next one on the conveyor belt, hugely impressive in the second-half.

'Birthday yesterday, that was a great day with grandkids and family. I had a specialist on Wednesday and it was really positive, he was really delighted and amazed at the progress I had made, from House-Brackmann (nerve grading scale) six to a four and he is really positive that within a year I'll get my eye back and be able to blink, so I won't have to tape it down at night.

'I still have to take juice to swallow and I have no taste in the side of my mouth and the whole side of the face is numb, so I have to drink through a straw still. He wasn't sure just how much that would progress because it's still really weak. But if sucking through a straw is worst case scenario then so be it. I won't be posting now because I won't see a specialist for another three months.

'A really good day and it just felt great to be back doing something when that seemed a million miles away. I didn't get out of bed for four weeks and couldn't speak for a month. I had some really dark days in this conservatory but I stayed positive and this too shall pass, everything passes, good or bad, everything comes and goes and sometimes you just have to dig in and get through it. But thanks for listening and see you all soon.'

Morrison made 47 appearances for Manchester City after joining from Huddersfield Town in 1998.

He helped guide the club to the old Division One via the play-offs in 1998-99 before winning promotion to the Premiership the following season.

Voted as Man City's third best captain ever in their official magazine, the Scot was named as a club ambassador in 2013.

Ramsay Hunt Syndrome is caused by a virus in the facial nerve and can lead to ipsilateral face paralysis, blistering rashes near the ear, severe earache and hearing loss.

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham continues his homecoming tour as he watches the cricket after investing in The Hundred franchise Birmingham Phoenix - hours after hero's welcome at his former football club
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham continues his homecoming tour as he watches the cricket after investing in The Hundred franchise Birmingham Phoenix - hours after hero's welcome at his former football club

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jude Bellingham continued his homecoming tour on Saturday by visiting Edgbaston, just a day after receiving a hero's welcome at his former football club Birmingham City.

The Real Madrid midfielder, who grew up in nearby Stourbridge, purchased a 1.2 per cent stake in The Hundred franchise Birmingham Phoenix earlier this year and has previously spoken about his love for cricket, saying he and his brother Jobe used to 'scrap' when playing it growing up and that it's now his 'favourite thing to watch outside football'.

On Saturday at the famous cricket ground, Bellingham was there to enjoy plenty of action, particularly in the first women's game. He watched on as Phoenix won their opening match of the women's competition in dramatic fashion, defeating Welsh Fire with just one ball remaining.

The England star was also on hand to present captain Donovan Ferreira with the coin for the toss in the subsequent men's match, although the 23-year-old wasn't able to inspire victory as the hosts slumped to defeat by Welsh Fire. England's newly confirmed Test captain Joe Root guided the visitors to victory with four balls remaining.

Hundreds of millions of pounds in private investment cash has been injected in The Hundred with all eight teams having been either partially or fully taken over by new owners as part of significant financial investment into the competition since last year. Upon announcing his own involvement with the franchise, Bellingham said: 'I feel like I owe the city something. And this feels like a good way.'

The Real Madrid midfielder, who grew up in nearby Stourbridge, purchased a 1.2 per cent stake in The Hundred franchise Birmingham Phoenix earlier this year

Bellingham was in attendance as Phoenix won their first match in the women's competition in dramatic fashion, defeating Welsh Fire with just one ball remaining

He as previously spoken about how he and his brother Jobe used to 'scrap' when playing it growing up and that it's now his 'favourite thing to watch outside football'

Upon announcing his own involvement with the franchise, Bellingham said: 'I feel like I owe the city something. And this feels like a good way'

The previous evening, Bellingham was welcomed back to his former club Birmingham City like a hero as he watched them triumph on penalties against Barcelona.

Barcelona had travelled to St Andrew's for a pre-season friendly against the Championship club, giving Blues fans plenty to cheer about as they were given a rare opportunity to see the LaLiga champions in action.

The occasion was made even more special for those inside St Andrew's when England superstar Bellingham, who began his glittering career at Birmingham before leaving to join Borussia Dortmund in 2020 and later Real Madrid in 2023, was unveiled at the start of the game.

Before kick-off, Birmingham City's official social media account showed Bellingham taking his seat and waving to fans in a touching video captioned: 'Jude. He's home.'

As he raised his arms aloft to greet the adoring fans, Blues supporters loudly bellowed 'Jude' to honour their former starlet and fervently chanted 'he's one of our own' in a special moment for the England midfielder at St Andrew's.

Bellingham is still enjoying some richly deserved time off after playing an integral role for England at the World Cup this summer and thus has not yet returned to the Spanish capital to begin the new season under Jose Mourinho.

The £113million midfielder cheered jubilantly as he watched his boyhood club triumph over Real Madrid's bitter rivals, winning on penalties after drawing 2-2 in normal time.

Bellingham was given a warm reception as he watched Birmingham defeat Barcelona

Bellingham posed for selfies with Birmingham fans who once cheered him on as a teenager

August Priske Flyger and John Solis were both on the scoresheet for the Blues, while Hamza Abdelkarim netted a brace for the Catalans.

Goalkeeper James Beadle was the hero in the shootout as he saved spot-kicks from Roony Bardghji and Brian Farinas, while Jordi Pesquer crashed his effort against the crossbar to hand Birmingham a 3-2 win on penalties.

Few clubs have a fonder view of an academy player than Birmingham City have of Bellingham, who at 23 has already become one of the best midfielders in world football.

Bellingham burst through the ranks at Birmingham as a youngster, starring for the U18s as a 14-year-old before making his debut for the U23s at the age of just 15.

The midfielder was then promoted to the Blues' senior squad for the 2019-20 season, becoming the youngest first-team player in the club's history at 16 years and 36 days old.

After making 41 appearances that campaign, Bellingham joined Borussia Dortmund for a £25m fee and became the youngest player ever to have his shirt retired by a professional club, with Birmingham permanently keeping his No 22 jersey out of action.

Despite arriving at St Andrew's in a white T-shirt, Bellingham finished the match wearing his retired No 22 Birmingham jersey, which appeared to bring the hosts luck as they pulled off a comeback to force the decisive penalty shootout.

Sports.title: Spain's 'down to earth' World Cup hero Marc Cucurella praised for wholesome interaction with postman as he lets him wear his winner's medal
Sports.content:
Spain's 'down to earth' World Cup hero Marc Cucurella praised for wholesome interaction with postman as he lets him wear his winner's medal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Spain star Marc Cucurella thrilled his local postman after the World Cup winner offered him the medal he won Stateside last month to wear after dropping off his deliveries.

The former Chelsea defender has been a Horsham resident for some years, moving there after a previous home was targeted by burglars shortly after his 2023 transfer to the west London club.

The West Sussex enclave provided a peaceful sanctuary for Cucurella and his young family, with locals frequently sharing their positive experiences on social media if they crossed the defender's path.

But few can claim the experience his postman Gary enjoyed during one of his last rounds for the departing Real Madrid star.

Sharing his story with Horsham's social media account, the postman said: 'Had the pleasure of chatting to local World Cup winner Marc Cucurella while delivering his post today.

'Very nice, down-to-earth guy. Let me hold his winners' medal.

Marc Cucurella was praised for his thoughtful interaction with his local postman in Horsham

Gary the postman was allowed to try on Cucurella's gold World Cup winners' medal

'I reckon I am the first Englishman to hold a World Cup winners' medal in 60 years.'

Fans were quick to show their support for Cucurella's once-in-a-lifetime gesture, with one commenting: 'The biggest and greatest accolade for any football player. And he was kind enough to share that.'

Another added: 'Amazing stuff. He sounds like a really nice guy.'

One chronicler of life in Horsham wrote: 'Amazing. We keep hearing great things and sorry to be losing him. Wishing him the best of luck in his new adventures'.

In the photograph, Cucurella showed off his new braided hairstyle, a notable departure from his iconic curls.

Switching up his look has been just one piece of the 28-year-old's post-World Cup celebrations, with the player also making good on his promise to ink the face of his manager Luis de la Fuente on his body.

Horsham's social media account has previously shared snapshots of Cucurella's life in the south of England, and cheered on their 'local boy' in Spain's World Cup final against Argentina.

Since becoming a resident in the market town, Cucurella and his family have slotted in seamlessly to local life, interacting with other parents at their children's schools and even becoming regular visitors to Indian restaurant Hen & Chicken.

Life in Horsham is likely one of the reasons that Cucurella's partner Claudia Rodriguez admitted that she was feeling mixed emotions about his move back to Spain to join Real Madrid.

Posting on Instagram after the £47.4m deal was announced, she wrote: 'I don't know how to say goodbye to my home.'

'Thank you to everyone who has been a part of this experience; I feel so lucky for everything we've shared these past years. I arrived with two babies and I'm leaving with two little boys and a British girl, and I don't know how I'm going to explain to them that Chelsea is no longer part of our lives.

'Everything we've experienced these past years has been a pure learning experience; we've lived through it all, but above all, we've enjoyed this journey. Thank you to everyone who has been a part of this chapter of our lives, thank you to my girls, whom I'm going to miss a lot, and thank you to every Blue I've met. I wish you all the best; London will always be Blue.'

Cucurella's partner Claudia Rodriguez spoke last month about her sadness at leaving England

Rodriguez's comments come in stark contrast to how she felt before the family moved into their latest house in England.

In the wake of the traumatising burglary, the influencer told Daily Mail Sport that she had been afraid to go to sleep.

'The security is one of things I'm more worried about,' Rodriguez admitted. 'It's very hard when you are not comfortable at your home.

'I'm scared to sleep alone with my kids, for example. So for today, the most important thing for me, I think, is the security of me and my family.'

Sports.title: 'I was F1 team-mates with Michael Schumacher and Lewis Hamilton – one is greatest of all time'
Sports.content:
'I was F1 team-mates with Michael Schumacher and Lewis Hamilton – one is greatest of all time'

Lewis Hamilton and Michael Schumacher share the record for the most Drivers' Championships, having competed against one another on numerous occasions

View 2 Images Nico Rosberg claims Lewis Hamilton is F1's GOAT (Image: Clive Mason/Getty Images)

Nico Rosberg believes Lewis Hamilton is the greatest-ever Formula 1 driver, even after competing alongside the iconic Michael Schumacher. The 41-year-old raced with Schumacher between 2010 and 2012 as he made a comeback to the track with Mercedes.

‌



Hamilton replaced the German when he retired for good, and his hugely successful career on the track ever since has kick-started a debate as to which of the two drivers has made the biggest impact on the sport. Rosberg spent two extra years with the British driver and has followed his career since he left F1 in 2016.

‌



The ex-Mercedes star spoke to Sky Sports Germany after the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix as he watched Hamilton soar to his record-extending 106th career win. This was the Brit's first win since he joined Ferrari in 2025 and Rosberg had nothing but praise for his former teammate.

‌



He said: "This is a fantastic day for the sport. It’s historic. He’s the greatest of all time. It’s great that he turned things around, because last year looked so dark and bleak.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Race cancelled just 24 hours after F1 confirm addition to calendar as statement released READ MORE :

"He was practically on his way home, could have said at any moment: I’m quitting. But he persevered, now feels comfortable in the car, and you can see a positive momentum everywhere."

‌



Presenter Peter Hardenacke noted that Rosberg made this huge statement while standing next to Michael's brother, Ralf Schumacher. After it was pointed out, the 41-year-old joked that he was merely trying to create a wedge between the two pundits.

Ralf previously claimed that Hamilton would never reach his brother's heights, stating that the German was "light years" ahead of the Brit. Discussing his sibling's legacy on Formel1.de’s YouTube channel, Ralf said: "I have to say quite honestly and not because he is my brother, maybe Max [Verstappen] can change that in his career if he really continues driving like this, but for me, it’s always what Michael brought with him.

View 2 Images Who is better - Hamilton or Schumacher? (Image: Glenn Dunbar/LAT Images)

‌



"There’s no one else like him; Lewis Hamilton will never come within light years, not from my point of view."

Schumacher won five straight titles with Ferrari in the early 2000s and competed with the likes of Ayrton Senna, Damon HIll, Sebastian Vettel and Fernando Alonso. Meanwhile, Hamilton's success came after he departed McLaren in 2012 when he won four consecutive championships from 2017 to 2020.

The Brit saw Max Verstappen stop his dominant run and he slowly fell out of title contention through the early 2020s. However, Hamilton is now just 50 points behind current F1 leader Kimi Antonelli and may fancy his chances at a record-breaking eighth title.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Vinicius Jr transfer trick set to be repeated as next three signings lined up
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Vinicius Jr transfer trick set to be repeated as next three signings lined up

Mikel Arteta and Arsenal are eyeing three more first-team additions

View 3 Images Arsenal are hoping to land Vinicius Junior (Image: Getty )

Arsenal have seemingly kicked into life as we enter the final month of the summer transfer window. Mikel Arteta’s men faced Girona in a pre-season friendly on Saturday evening - but the focus was mainly on the club's activity off the field.

‌



That’s because the Gunners have been closely linked with several big-name targets in recent days, including Vinicius Junior of Real Madrid. The Los Blancos superstar would represent the first genuinely marquee addition of the window for sporting director Andrea Berta, having been given the green light financially to bring in the forward.

‌



Until now, Berta has only signed Piero Hincapie on a permanent basis for £34.5million, third-choice goalkeeper Illan Meslier and £34m Leandro Trossard replacement Christos Tzolis. Ahead of the transfer window’s closure on September 1, Mirror Football brings you the latest news from the Emirates Stadium.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Three signings lined up

View 3 Images Bruno Guimaraes is reportedly close to being signed (Image: Getty )

Arsenal are reportedly eyeing three more signings this summer. The Athletic reported on Saturday that Vinicius is Arteta’s top transfer target to strengthen the attack.

‌



An agreement between the Brazilian and Arsenal is expected to be found on personal terms if Real Madrid don’t match his demands and the forward opts not to renew at the Bernabeu. The report adds that, whether Vinicius signs or not, the north Londoners will bring in a new winger before the window shuts.

Arsenal will also seek a new midfielder, understood to be Bruno Guimaraes, after reportedly agreeing a £77m deal with Newcastle. Finally, The Athletic states a central defender is being pursued in an effort to cover the injured William Saliba in the coming months.

Vinicius transfer trick repeat

View 3 Images Ferran Torres is on Arsenal's radar (Image: FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



The transfer links with Vinicius seemingly came out of nowhere last weekend. Yet, Berta is understood to have kept an eye on the 26-year-old winger’s contract situation for some time before making his approach, having seen Vinicius enter the final year of his deal.

Now, Arsenal are reportedly considering employing a similar method in their pursuit of another forward - Barcelona’s Ferran Torres - who is also due to become a free agent next summer, as it stands.

Spanish outlet Estadio Deportivo claims the Gunners have enquired about the Spain striker, who scored the decisive goal in the World Cup final last month. Barcelona want to extend Torres' contract, which is due to expire in June next year.

Article continues below

But negotiations are yet to produce an agreement, increasing pressure on Barcelona to cash in rather than risk losing the 26-year-old for nothing next summer. That, similarly to the Vinicius situation, plays directly into Arsenal’s hands as they can offer a lower transfer fee. Torres can play on either wing or through the middle, with his versatility making this potential signing an alluring one.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta directly pressed on Vinicius Jr before ending Arsenal press conference suddenly
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta directly pressed on Vinicius Jr before ending Arsenal press conference suddenly

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta was asked about Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr during his post-match press conference on Saturday evening in Girona

View 2 Images Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr. continues to be linked with Arsenal (Image: Icon Sport via Getty Images)

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has refused to be drawn on whether the Gunners will secure the signing of Vinicius Junior this summer — abruptly bringing his post-match press conference to a close after being quizzed about the Brazilian star.

‌



Arteta's side are understood to be weighing up a move for the Real Madrid winger, with the 26-year-old seen as a prime candidate to bolster Arsenal's left flank — widely regarded as a vulnerability in their attack — as they look to cement their position as Premier League champions.

‌



Vinicius Jr. netted 22 goals and provided 14 assists in 53 appearances for Los Blancos last season — despite the Spanish giants enduring a disappointing campaign. With negotiations over a contract extension at the Santiago Bernabeu having reportedly hit a wall, it could represent a golden opportunity for the Gunners to land one of football's most electrifying attacking talents.

‌



Max Dowman oozes class as new Arsenal partnership unlocked in Girona win – 5 talking points READ MORE :

Arsenal could still add another blockbuster signing aside from Vinicius Jr or Bruno Guimaraes READ MORE :

Arteta was asked about a potential deal for the very first time following Arsenal's 4-1 pre-season friendly victory over Girona on Saturday.

When pressed on whether supporters could expect further additions to the squad before the new season gets underway, he said: "Well, we are really active, trying to improve and evolve the team. That's clear.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else. And you can just see it.

"The transfer market and our opponents, what we are doing, we won't sit still. And we are very ambitious in what we want to do."

View 2 Images Vinicius Jr is being linked with a big-money move to Arsenal (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



The Spaniard was subsequently asked, in the final question, whether Vinicius Jr. would be arriving.

"Thank you so much," the 44-year-old responded with a smirk before departing.

Recent reports from Spanish outlet Marca suggest that Jose Mourinho's outfit have tabled a final offer to the Brazil international.

‌



It is understood that no further salary enhancements or additional rounds of talks are expected, and should he turn down the proposal, Madrid will seek to cash in this summer.

However, the coming days will prove crucial and football.london understands that while Arteta's side have growing confidence, the final call rests with Vinicius Jr.

Real may also need to generate funds, as reports indicate they are eyeing a £102m swoop for RB Leipzig winger Yan Diomande. Sports.title: Amad and Leny Yoro in total agreement after JJ Gabriel makes Man Utd debut
Sports.content:
Amad and Leny Yoro in total agreement after JJ Gabriel makes Man Utd debut

JJ Gabriel made his Manchester United debut at the age of 15 in the latter stages of their 2-1 pre-season win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm on Saturday

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel made his Manchester United debut against Atletico Madrid (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

JJ Gabriel has sparked excitement among the ranks at Manchester United after making his senior debut in their pre-season win over Atletico Madrid on Saturday. The 15-year-old came off the bench in Stockholm to play the final eight minutes of United's 2-1 comeback win.

‌



Bryan Mbeumo may have been the match-winner, scoring a penalty and bundling in a second to complete the turnaround. But Gabriel was undoubtedly the main talking point after manager Michael Carrick brought him on to replace Mbeumo late on.

‌



There has been a great deal of excitement around the young forward for some time, following 26 goals in 26 games in the Under-18 Premier League last season, and his potential is obvious.

‌



"More to come little bro," wrote Amad on Instagram after the full-time whistle in a post re-shared by Gabriel himself.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Michael Carrick drops clear hint over three Man Utd transfers after Atletico Madrid win READ MORE :

Bryan Mbeumo inspires Man Utd win vs Atletico Madrid as transfer hint drops - 6 talking points READ MORE :

There was also some praise from United defender Leny Yoro. "He's a really good player," he said. "Still really young, still a lot to learn, a lot to improve. He's really humble, still working, so I'm happy for him to get his first minutes, so I hope for him it's going to continue like that."

‌



Yoro himself made his debut for Lille aged 16 and joined United for £52million, becoming the most expensive player under the age of 18 in the history of the game two years ago.

"I can see myself," Yoro added before offering some advice. "[I would say] stay humble, just want to work, and this is what we need in the team, even for the young guys.

"They're all doing really well, and JJ is one of them, so I hope he's going to learn a lot, continue like that, improve, yeah. But he's really good, a good player."

‌



View 2 Images JJ Gabriel came on to replace Bryan Mbeumo in the 82nd minute (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Gabriel trained with the first team last season and will hope that Carrick's presence as manager can aid his progression in the 2026/27 campaign. With some senior players yet to return following the World Cup, there has been a youthful look to the United team in pre-season, with Gabriel one of a number of academy players hoping to catch the eye.

Shea Lacey started and won the penalty which Mbeumo converted to make it 1-1, while Jack Fletcher - a half-time substitute for Amad - intercepted the ball and provided the assist for the Cameroon international's winner.

‌



Carrick was happy with what he saw from the mixture of young and experienced players. “The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company," he told MUTV.

"Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Sports.title: Max Dowman oozes class as new Arsenal partnership unlocked in Girona win – 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Max Dowman oozes class as new Arsenal partnership unlocked in Girona win – 5 talking points

GIRONA 1-4 ARSENAL: Max Dowman grabbed the headlines as Mikel Arteta's side put in a strong pre-season display against Spanish opposition

View 4 Images Max Dowman and Christos Tzolis were on target for Mikel Arteta's Arsenal against Girona

Arsenal strode to a 4-1 victory over Girona in their first official clash of pre-season with Max Dowman grabbing a goal and assist. Kai Havertz, Christos Tzolis and Gabriel Jesus were also on target with Ethan Nwaneri and Riccardo Calafiori making attacking contributions, but it was Dowman that stole the show.

‌



The opening goal arrived just after the quarter-of-an-mark as Havertz finished calmly after a brilliant piece of skill and pass from Dowman. A second arrived on the 30th minute when Arsenal broke through Girona's press courtesy of an excellent Ethan Nwaneri pass into Riccardo Calafiori.

‌



The Italian moved the ball out wide to Tzolis with the summer signing using his quick feet to gain a yard of space with his effort nestling in the far corner after a deflection. Girona did pull one back from a corner early into the second period with Arnau Martinez heading past Kepa Arrizabalaga.

‌



Arsenal could still add another blockbuster signing aside from Vinicius Jr or Bruno Guimaraes READ MORE :

Arsenal star refused to go on pre-season tour to force through summer transfer READ MORE :

However, that deficit was at one for minutes as Dowman and Jesus both scored in the space of two minutes. The latter took advantage of an error to poke home while Dowman fired an effort into the corner with his left foot from just outside of the box.

Arteta brought on several fringe and academy players during the second half with goalmouth action minimal as the final whistle edged closer. Nonetheless, it was a very good workout for several Arsenal stars and a confident showing in front of goal.

Here, Mirror Football takes a look at the biggest talking points from the victory.

‌



Dowman's busy display

Max Dowman was more or less involved in every piece of good play by Arsenal in the opening 45 minutes.

It was his smart turn that opened up a huge gap in Girona's midfield for the first goal and his pass was perfectly weighted into Havertz with the German taking one touch before sliding home.

Midway through the first half, he showed his awareness at the other end by intercepting a pass inside the defensive third as Girona threatened. He went on a jinking run just before half-time before falling to the floor after being crowded out by Girona players in the penalty area, but the referee dismissed appeals for a spot-kick.

‌



It wasn't the best start to the half for Dowman with a poor decision made when he received the ball in the final third. Viktor Gyokeres was in acres of space on the other side of the pitch and the pass was on but he opted to dribble forward before losing possession which resulted in the Swede screaming at him for not passing.

View 4 Images Max Dowman scored a great goal as Arsenal beat Girona

Dowman later got on the score sheet himself as he drove an effort into the back of the net from 20 yards after another precise forward pass by Myles Lewis-Skelly. The 16-year-old was back defending immediately after that and made a crucial interception but just moments later needed to be bailed out by Kepa Arrizabalaga after a mishit back pass.

‌



He was brought off on the hour-mark with cameras capturing him deep in discussion with Arteta on the sidelines. While he is not the finished article, Dowman's quality was clearly on display and he looks set for a breakout season at Emirates Stadium.

New partnership unlocked

Due to the sheer amount of squad depth at his diposal, Arteta can choose to deploy certain players with others in order to develop partnerships. Based on the first 45 minutes in Spain, expect to see Christos Tzolis and Riccardo Calafiori linking up frequently.

The latter is an unorthodox full-back and will often find himself in central areas. That was the case for Arsenal's second goal as he drove into Girona's half after receiving a sharp forward pass from Nwaneri with Tzolis later picked out on the touchline.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Calafiori continued his run forward which occupied defenders and opened up space for the Greek international to cut inside and send an effort into the far corner, albeit via a deflection.

Defensive struggles

Arsenal were not at their defensive best in Girona with substitute goalkeeper Illian Meslier forced into a number of saves. It is worth noting those came after a number of alterations but even at full strength, the Gunners didn't look that solid.

‌



Early into the clash, Ben White was caught out and left chasing Girona players while there were a number of sloppy passes among their own backline.

Perhaps what would have angered Arteta most was conceding from a corner with Arnau Martinez jumping unmarked to head home. Riccardo Calafiori is arguably the only regular starter that was deployed from the off but Arteta's favoured back four is unlikely to be deployed early in the season.

William Saliba has a back injury and Jurrien Timber looks set to be managed carefully. Gabriel Magalhaes will also likely be monitored as he has played a lot of minutes in the last few years.

‌



Signing a defender is not the priority but it is clear why there have been links to a number of cental defenders.

Early substitutions

It was somewhat surprising to see Viktor Gyokeres, Kai Havertz and Piero Hincapie taken off after the first drinks break midway around the 30th minute.

View 4 Images Kai Havertz was one of three Arsenal stars to play just 30 minutes against Girona

‌



However, it makes perfect sense considering that trio all reached the World Cup last-32 and were therefore late arrivals to pre-season. Gabriel Martinelli and Magalhaes were eliminated in the following round and based on this, will likely be eased back into action.

Arteta has faced criticism for overplaying the likes of Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka but it looks as though he is being extra careful now especially after a number of key players struggled with fitness issues during the second half of the season.

Guimaraes transfer incentive

Regardless of the strong performance, the need to wrap up a deal for Bruno Guimaraes promptly was clear before the pre-season clash had even got underway.

‌



Arteta named a strong starting XI but, on paper, the balance in midfield was not the best. Lewis-Skelly, Havertz and Nwaneri are all talented footballers in their own right but the midfield dynamic did leave Arsenal open at times.

Arteta does not have too much choice, however, with Martin Odegaard, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino all still on holiday after the World Cup.

Brazil duo Gabriel Martinelli and Magalhaes have made their returns which means Bruno Guimaraes' minimum rest period is also due to be up. However, it seems as though he will be heading to Arsenal's training camp now as opposed to Newcastle's with an £80m deal agreed.

‌



View 4 Images Bruno Guimaraes looks set to join Arsenal from Newcastle United

Arteta needed this signing wrapped up quickly - simply because Guimaraes will be required for the opening few weeks of the season and also to have plenty of training sessions under Arteta and with his new team-mates.

Considering that Christian Norgaard, who was sat among the substitutes in Girona, is set to join Everton, the Guimaraes to Arsenal deal is now expected to ramp up.

Article continues below

The Community Shield against Manchester City takes place in just over two weeks and Guimaraes ideally needs to be starting as the likes of Phil Foden, Rayan Cherki and Elliot Anderson present more of a threat than Girona.

Sports.title: Arsenal could still add another blockbuster signing aside from Vinicius Jr or Bruno Guimaraes
Sports.content:
Arsenal could still add another blockbuster signing aside from Vinicius Jr or Bruno Guimaraes

Arsenal are hoping to sign Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior, but that has not stopped them from working on another transfer

View 2 Images Arsenal want to sign Vinicius Junior (Image: DeFodi Images, DeFodi Images via Getty Images)

Arsenal are working to sign Vinicius Junior from Real Madrid but remain in the market for Atletico Madrid star Julian Alvarez. The Gunners are said to remain interested in the Argentina star despite being ready to make a mega-money move for his La Liga rival.

‌



Atleti ace Alvarez has long been linked to the Gunners, who were reportedly willing to offer Viktor Gyokeres in a player-plus-cash arrangement. Diego Simeone's side have been reluctant to sell their star, with the forward particularly interested in a move to Barcelona.

‌



Nevertheless, the prospect of an incredible summer double deal seeing Arsenal pluck Vinicius and Alvarez from the Spanish capital appears to be on the cards. Signing either would be a significant statement from the north London side ahead of their Premier League title defence.

‌



According to The Independent, Arsenal continue to pursue a deal for Alvarez. It has also been suggested Arsenal are confident about their chances of securing Vinicius.

Meanwhile, a transfer to bring Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal from Newcastle seems to be drawing closer, with his future potentially settled within the coming week.

Arsenal reach transfer agreement with medical to come next in major Bruno Guimaraes boost READ MORE :

New Newcastle boss makes Bruno Guimaraes stance clear amid Arsenal offer READ MORE :

The arrival of those players would see Mikel Arteta significantly improve his depth at the Emirates. The Spaniard would be able to choose a front three of Vinicius, Alvarez, Bukayo Saka, with the likes of Eberechi Eze, Noni Madueke and new signing Christos Tzolis available for rotation.

‌



Arteta recently made it crystal clear he needed to strengthen his squad with additional elite players if they were to continue challenging across four competitions.

He said: "From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level. That is going to require a better squad, better individual.

"We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully, very soon, we can start to put things in a very concrete way."

‌



View 2 Images Arsenal are still working on a move for Julian Alvarez (Image: Carl Recine, Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arteta continued: "This has to be the start and this has to be the standard. Excellence has to be our standard and this has to drive to attack the future.

‌



"The way we behave daily with more and more determination and ambition because we've shown that we've got it. Now we have to show that we belong to this level. We want to increase and take this football club to a different dimension.

"My ambition is that daily we nail the standards and the requirements to be better the following day. That is the thing that we have to control, and maintain that ambition, that discipline, that commitment and that positive energy through 11 months. That is the responsibility that we all have. If we all achieve that, we are going to be in a really strong position in May."

Sports.title: Chelsea squad's immediate reaction to Mykhailo Mudryk bombshell and imminent return
Sports.content:
Chelsea squad's immediate reaction to Mykhailo Mudryk bombshell and imminent return

Mykhailo Mudryk can officially return to football, and his Chelsea team-mates have made their feelings perfectly clear

View 2 Images Levi Colwill was one of many Chelsea stars to send a message to Mykhailo Mudryk (Image: (Photo by Visionhaus/Getty Images))

Several Chelsea stars have issued messages of support to Mykhailo Mudryk after his doping ban was lifted. The 25-year-old has not played for the Blues since November 2024 after testing positive for meldonium and being handed a four-year suspension by the FA

‌



Earlier this week, a statement was released by English football's governing body which stated that that disciplinary proceedings against the Ukrainian had been resolved. A provisional ban was placed on Mudryk a month on from his failed test.

‌



During his time out, an appeal was lodged with the Court of Arbitration for Sport while confirmation of a hearing being set arrived in May of last year with 'written submissions' also exchanged. However, the situation has now been resolved with Mudryk posting on social media after the decision was made official.

‌



Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso gives Mykhailo Mudryk update as winger handed green light to return READ MORE :

His Chelsea team-mates Levi Colwill and Reece James led tributes by reposting his official statement to their Instagram stories. Romeo Lavia, Nicolas Jackson, Robert Sanchez, and Malo Gusto all followed their lead.

Meanwhile, former teammates including Ben Chilwell, Marc Cucurella, and Christopher Nkunku, alongside Cole Palmer, Enzo Fernandez, Moises Caicedo, Pedro Neto, and Wesley Fofana, were amongst the 1.5 million users to 'like' the Ukrainian's post.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Almost 60,000 users also flooded the comment section with messages of support. It is understood that Mudryk will now travel to Hong Kong to link up with the Chelsea squad ahead of Wednesday's friendly against Juventus.

Speaking to journalists at the Accor Stadium in Sydney, Australia, on Saturday, following a 2-1 defeat to Tottenham Hotspur, Alonso described the winger as a 'special' player, while tempering expectations regarding any immediate return to action.

"We are happy for him, especially for him," said the Blues manager. "Probably, we are not able to understand what he has been through in this time and how does he feel at the moment with the things that he had to cope with.

‌



"We want that he feels part of a team, because he has been training on his own for a long time, and that we have the support from everyone, from the club, from the teammates, from the staff, and for sure it will take time. So once he is with us, we will see how things develop."

On Mudryk's future, Alonso said: "We need to see, it's too early to tell, to see how he is in terms of fitness, in terms of this game time that you need to be involved again, so it's still early to tell."

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso's latest Chelsea press conference was dominated by Mykhailo Mudryk

‌



The Chelsea boss added: "We have the Mudryk that [we had], it will take time, but once there is a change, things start moving, and for him it's a massive change. So he trained on his own every day, and I think it had to be really, really hard, because he wanted to play football.

"He wanted to be part of a team, and he was not allowed to do that for such a long time. So once this big change has happened, now things will move on, and afterwards we will see if it's quicker, if it's slower, but we need to be aware of that."

Reflecting on Mudryk's abilities as a footballer, Alonso said: "Yeah, I remember watching him in Shakhtar, the impact he had, how quick he is, how good in one-on-one situations, how he could create a lot of situations on his own, and he's a special player, but he will take time for sure."

Article continues below

"To be honest, we were not expecting to have this great news at this moment, so we are very happy. We feel that he will be working with us."

Sports.title: "Phenomenal horseman" praised for role in brilliant Goodwood week for Wathnan Racing
Sports.content:
"Phenomenal horseman" praised for role in brilliant Goodwood week for Wathnan Racing

Hamad Al Jehani took two big Goodwood prizes with his thoroughbreds, the Coral-backed Golden Mile and Stewards Cup. The team's seven winners were Wild Blossom, Flora Of Bermuda, Exclusive Code, Archivist, Silver Lake, Hopewell Rock and Evening Saigon

View 2 Images Trainer Hamad Al Jehani (left) with several members of the Wathnan Racing team after Evening Saigon won the Coral Stewards' Cup (Image: Andrew Matthews/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

"Phenomenal horseman" Hamad Al Jehani was praised for his role in a big week for Wathnan Racing at the 2026 Qatar Goodwood Festival.

‌



The trainer sent out Evening Saigon to land the Coral Stewards Cup on Saturday, just a day after fellow 16-1 shot Archivist bagged another big handicap on Friday, the Golden Mile with the same sponsors.

‌



The pair were among seven winners for the owners over the five days, scooping just over £218,000 in prize money from their races alone.

‌



"Hamad has turned up and won two of the hardest handicaps to win all year," said Wathnan's racing advisor Richard Brown.

"We plot these and work as a team – when these results come off, it’s just fantastic for Wathnan and what we are all about.

Top jockey Jim Crowley retires at 48 after horror fall at York led to five operations READ MORE :

“If you look at Hamad’s statistics since he started training, they match up with the best trainers in the country. He’s a phenomenal horseman and was a very good rider himself. He’s very modest about it but he showjumped to a good level.

‌



"We all work very closely together and to pull this off is huge for everybody involved.”

Wild Blossom got the ball rolling in the Alice Keppell Conditions Stakes on Wednesday and Flora Of Bermuda, Exclusive Code, Silver Lake and Hopewell Rock also hit the target.

James Doyle picked Evening Saigon from the three Wathnan Racing had in contention in the Coral Stewards Cup and although the sprinter used plenty of energy before the start, he had enough left to see off Stratusnine on the far side.

‌



Mitbaahy was closing the pair down and took third in Saturday's feature, with Completely Random a close-up fourth under the meeting's leading rider Ryan Moore.

View 2 Images Evening Saigon (red cap) won the Coral Stewards Cup (Image: Getty Images)

"I am very happy for Evening Saigon and very happy for the team," said Hamad Al Jehani. "He performed very well at Royal Ascot and it was the right decision from the management to keep him for the Stewards’ Cup.

‌



“It’s really important for us and it’s a really important race for the season. I’m very happy and thanks to James for giving the horse a great ride.

“It’s not easy to be competitive with the best trainers in the world but we try our best and I think we are building in a very good way, with great help from the management. Hopefully, we will improve year by year and we can make Wathnan be in the winner’s enclosure more and more.”

Handlers Archie Watson, William Haggas, Andrew Balding, Karl Burke and George Boughey all saddled winners for the team across the week.

"Obviously I was very deflated last year (at the meeting) so the memo was we need to do better and that’s everyone, including me as well,” Evening Saigon's rider James Doyle said.

"He’s not an easy conveyance, setting off he was that well in himself he tried to get rid of me the first few strides but that was great."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
