World.title: Raul Meel's anniversary exhibition on display at the Poco Ajamaja gallery
World.content:
Dedicated to Raul Meel's 85th birthday, the exhibition "Concret" is open at the Poco Ajamaja gallery. It traces the artist's journey from his first groundbreaking experiments in the late 1960s to the present day.

Exhibition curator Jaan Heinsoo says the exhibition focuses on concrete poetry – works that combine poetry and visual art. In concrete poetry, meaning is not only derived from words but also from visual experience, the rhythmic structure of words and signs, the interplay of colors, repetition, and silence.

"The exhibition is a retrospective of the artist's life's work spanning more than fifty years, presenting a cross-section of the various eras, facets, and techniques of Raul Meel's creative journey from 1970s typewriter drawings to a painting from the "Epic of Bristles" series created this year," Heinsoo explained.

"A large portion of the works were produced over the past year, yet the ideas and motifs largely originate from earlier creative periods."

Meel (b. 1941) is one of Estonia's best-known avant-garde artists and among Europe's leading practitioners of conceptual art and concrete poetry. He has participated in more than 600 group exhibitions and over 100 solo exhibitions, and remains the only Estonian artist to have received a prize at a major international biennial.

World.title: Teachers, NGO call for more emphasis on global education in school curricula
World.content:
NGO Mondo has said Estonia's education system should place greater emphasis on global citizenship, and the chair of the Estonian History and Civics Teachers' Association agrees. The Ministry of Education says that global education competencies are already included in the current curricula.

Global education, knowledge of how global issues affect the daily lives of individuals, communities and society, and how everyone can influence the world, has been promoted in Estonia for 15 years.

Schools can choose elective courses, take part in themed weeks and projects, and such content has been integrated into various subjects, but according to those involved, this has been done in a fragmented way.

Meelis Niine, project manager at the non-profit organization Mondo, told ERR that in the future global education could be described more clearly in the general sections of the national curricula and in subject syllabi, and that global citizenship competencies could also be set out more specifically.

"If there were a separate emphasis specifically on global citizenship competencies, it would help make global education a clearer and more integral part of formal education. What do I mean by global citizenship competencies? On the one hand, it means that young people should understand different global challenges, their local dimension, and how global challenges are reflected locally. At the same time, it is also important to care about these issues and to take active action," he said.

Niine thinks this is a weak point because many young people in Estonia may be fairly well informed about global issues, but they make relatively few active choices in their daily lives or engage in civic activism.

Madli-Maria Naulainen, chair of the Estonian History and Civics Teachers' Association, said that global education is certainly already part of civics classes, but that does not mean it could not receive greater emphasis.

"At the moment, a great deal depends on the individual teacher – some choose to address these topics more, others less," Naulainen explained. "I very much agree that the topic of global education should be highlighted more and should not depend solely on teachers' individual choices."

According to the chair, the association has worked closely with Mondo all along and has helped distribute the educational materials created by Mondo for use in civics lessons.

"That line of cooperation certainly exists now, but in a situation where teachers can choose which topics they use to achieve particular learning outcomes, a specific section in the curriculum would provide a better guarantee that everyone has gained some knowledge in this area," Naulainen argued.

Ministry: Schools have a lot of autonomy

Adviser on general education policy at the Ministry of Education and Research, Mare Oja, said there is no contradiction in the current situation. The principles of global education are already included in the national curriculum's general competencies and core values.

"We have universal human and social values, which include both solidarity, civic engagement and seeing oneself as a citizen of the world. In Estonia, the national curriculum is a general document on the basis of which schools develop their own curricula, and our schools have a great deal of autonomy," she said.

She added that in upper secondary school, 63 of the 96 courses are determined by the national curriculum, while schools design the remaining third themselves, creating their own profile and deciding what they want to explore in greater depth. Some focus on economics education, others on financial literacy, and some on global education. As a result, the situation is diverse.

"In fact, all these principles are already included. Specific topics are covered in geography and civics. For example, when we talk about cultural diversity, foreign languages, language and literature, and certainly history all support that," Oja said.

Teachers: Schools may lack broader perspective

Madli-Maria Naulainen of the History and Civics Teachers' Association noted that although several school subjects touch on global education, what may be lacking is a broader perspective that would help students understand globalization and give them an idea of what development cooperation is and why it is necessary.

"In today's globalized world, it is inevitable that we must keep up with these issues. Understanding and solidarity toward others are also areas that could certainly be better addressed through these topics," Naulainen said.

Maari Ross, adviser at the Humanitarian Aid Bureau of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said some European countries also look to Estonia's education system for inspiration, but at the same time, the issue of fragmentation still needs to be addressed.

"One important area is regional support and cooperation networks. In Estonia, we actually have several very strong schools and competence centers working on global education. The question is how to ensure and improve the sharing of their experience with others. Another important area is research and evaluating the impact of global education – how to increase the interest of Estonian researchers in studying global education," Ross said.

According to Naulainen, civics is expected to provide good citizenship education, while in reality the subject has a fairly limited place in schools.

"Civics as a subject is taught only in the sixth, ninth and 12th grades. We have discussed whether the volume of civics education should perhaps be expanded, because expectations have increased and there are visible signs of polarization and extremism in society," the association's chair said.

At the end of last year, stakeholders in the field produced a vision document, and on that basis they are now moving toward drafting an action plan.

World.title: Temporary basketball courts open in August on Tallinn's Freedom Square
World.content:
Three public 3x3 basketball courts will be set up on Tallinn's Freedom Square and will be open to the public from August 4–14.

The City of Tallinn is installing ball bins filled with basketballs at the courts, operating on a "take, play, return" basis.

World.title: PPA: Nõmme migrant case is not an isolated incident
World.content:
The Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) detained 15 suspected illegal migrants on Thursday in a Tallinn suburb, but said similar incidents have occurred elsewhere. The agency asked the public to be vigilant but "reasonable," stressing "not everyone with a different skin color is problematic."

The PPA has said the migrants have likely entered the European Union after illegally crossing the Latvian-Belarus border. Politicians and the security services say the route is part of a "hybrid attack" by the Minsk authorities with Russian support.

The uptick in migrants in Estonia is likely caused by additional checks on Poland's northern and western borders to stop people smugglers traveling to Germany. The destination has now changed to Finland and Scandinavia, the PPA has said. Over 80 have been caught in the last two weeks, compared to 39 last year.

When police arrived at the scene in a suburb in the south of the capital, they initially detained 12 people. Three others had already left the area, but authorities caught them a few hours later.

Neighbors alerted the police after noticing people whose appearance and behavior stood out in the neighborhood.

The migrants were detained outside the guesthouse. The building's owner told ERR that he had not been aware of them staying at the property, although the house was later found in disarray. The owner said they had no security camera footage or other evidence confirming that the people had stayed at their accommodation.

Police operation on Tallinn's Nõmme district on Thursday. Source: Private collection

Local residents told ERR that even late in the evening, after 11 p.m., plainclothes police officers could be seen around the house. Dogs were used in the search early in the evening, and drones were also deployed. Searches were also carried out in a nearby forest.

Indrek Aru, head of the Border Guard Bureau of the North Prefecture, said on Friday that no additional people were found during the late-night searches.

"If there is reason to believe that there may be people somewhere who have no legal basis to stay in Estonia, then naturally we verify such information. That is what we did yesterday in Nõmme. When we detained a larger group of people in the area who presumably had no legal basis to stay here, we naturally looked around more broadly, and that is how those operations were carried out," he said.

However, the police are not certain that all 15 people detained on Thursday belonged to the same group.

"There is obviously reason to look for those connections, and that work is still ongoing," Aru added.

The PPA has not disclosed its communication with the property owner. However, Aru stressed that accommodation providers are obliged to verify whether third-country nationals arriving to use their services have a legal basis to stay in the country by checking their documents.

"Naturally, verifying and complying with those requirements is more complicated in the case of guest apartments offered for short-term rental," Aru acknowledged.

Fifteen suspected illegal migrants were arrested in Tallinn's Nõmme district on July 30. It is assumed they were trying to travel on to Finland. Source: Helen Wright/ OSM/ Datawrapper

He urged owners of rental properties to notify the police if a large number of people arrive at their guest apartment who may not have a legal basis to stay, or if they appear exhausted and as though they have arrived from difficult conditions.

Although the group of migrants detained in Nõmme attracted considerable attention, it was not an exceptional case for the PPA.

"We have also discovered groups of foreign nationals who presumably do not have a valid legal basis to stay at other accommodation establishments and in other districts," Aru said. "What happened in Nõmme is not an isolated case; we have had a couple of similar incidents. The Nõmme case simply attracted greater public attention this time because a significantly larger police response was involved."

Police have received unfounded reports based on skin color

Minister of Interior Igor Taro (Eesti 200) has also urged people to report suspicious individuals.

However, the Police have already received unfounded reports about people based solely on their skin color.

"I have heard about a few cases where people drew our attention to someone and even approached us on the street, saying they had seen someone who was probably staying in the country illegally or without a legal basis. It later turned out that the person had all the necessary documents, was completely law-abiding, and even spoke Estonian," Aru said.

"I would certainly recommend maintaining a reasonable approach," the PPA representative stressed. "Even today we are seeing well-intentioned reports, but it is important to remain reasonable when making notifications. Not everyone with a different skin color is problematic. This should be viewed in a balanced way."

A police van at the Port of Tallinn. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

The PPA is also carrying out additional checks across the country, not only Tallinn and Harju County where the main ports and airports are located.

Aru said police resources have not been exhausted.

"There is no reason for people in Estonia to worry. If you call 112, the police will come, and they do so quite quickly. Estonia has a very good emergency response time. When migration pressure increases, cooperation between countries also increases," he said.

Aru explained that this type of illegal migration is being facilitated by the authorities in Russia and Belarus.

"Naturally, people in the countries of origin of migration are looking for a better life or have other reasons for setting out. But the fact that they have chosen such a route and end up entering our visa area illegally clearly shows that this is a hybrid attack by Belarus," he said.

Migrants have been crossing the Belarusian border into Latvia, Lithuania and Poland since 2021, in what European officials say is a manufactured hybrid attack orchestrated by the Belarusian regime. The issues started after the EU sanctioned Belarusian leader Alexander Lukashenko.

Migrants cross the border and then try to travel onto western or northern Europe. Last year, Germany and Poland introduced checks on their borders in an attempt to stop people smugglers. Over the past year, several drivers transporting migrants have been stopped at the Polish-Lithuanian border, and now the flow has redirected northwards, the PPA said on Wednesday.

World.title: Chevron CFO bullish on Iraq after West Qurna 2, Nassiriya agreements
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Chevron boasts “significant potential” to expand its activities in Iraq over the next decade, according to Chief Financial Officer Eimear Bonner, highlighting the US oil company’s increasing trust in the country’s energy sector after recent deals with Baghdad.

Speaking to Bloomberg, Bonner said that Iraq remained one of Chevron’s top priority markets for future production expansion after the signing of preliminary agreements to pursue negotiations on the massive West Qurna 2 and Nassiriya oil fields.

She added that Chevron has been encouraged by its interaction with Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi and Iraq’s Ministry of Oil while discussions continue and that the corporation is also collaborating with Baghdad on diverse crude export routes to boost Iraq’s long-term energy security.

The statements bolster rising trust among foreign energy corporations after Al-Zaidi’s visit to the United States earlier this month, during which Iraq inked more than $60 billion in investment deals covering energy, infrastructure, banking, and technology.

World.title: Syria joins Saudi Arabia, Jordan in warning Iraq over Iran-backed militias
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Syria has joined Saudi Arabia and Jordan in warning Baghdad that strikes conducted from Iraqi soil against neighboring nations may result in military strikes against the armed groups responsible, according to Syrian military officials cited by regional media.

According to Al Jazeera and the US-funded Al Hurra, a senior Syrian military source said that Damascus will react to any strikes from Iraq by attacking the “terrorist militias” involved inside Iraqi territory.

The purported warning comes amid a steep increase in regional tensions after US-Saudi bombings against Iran-backed militias in Iraq in retaliation for drone assaults on Saudi oil installations, which Riyadh said were conducted from Iraqi territory.

The Iraqi government has frequently said that it would not allow Iraqi land to be used as a launchpad for attacks on neighboring nations.

Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi recently issued an order establishing a comprehensive security strategy aimed at enhancing state authority and preventing armed organizations from endangering regional security.

The new threat puts further pressure on Baghdad, as more neighboring nations indicate they may take direct action if cross-border assaults continue.

Iraqi authorities have attempted to prevent such a situation, claiming that security activities should be overseen by the Iraqi government rather than foreign forces.

Several Iran-backed organizations operating inside Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) are at the heart of the conflict, including Kataib Hezbollah, Asaib Ahl al-Haq, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada.

While the PMF is technically part of Iraq’s security system, some of its sections have strong links to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and have been accused by regional governments of carrying out strikes outside of Baghdad’s jurisdiction.

For Iraq, the diplomatic stakes go beyond security.

Baghdad has been attempting to reestablish ties with Syria as part of greater regional economic integration, including talks on resurrecting the old Iraq-Syria oil pipeline to the Mediterranean, which is considered strategically crucial for diversifying Iraq’s export routes outside the Gulf.

The purported Syrian warning comes at a critical moment for Al-Zaidi’s administration, which has spent recent months bolstering relations with Washington, Ankara, Riyadh, and Damascus while portraying Iraq as a secure destination for global investment.

The mounting threats from neighboring Arab governments highlight the importance of Baghdad demonstrating its ability to prevent armed groups from conducting strikes independent of the state.

Failure to do so risks increasing regional military tensions and jeopardizing Iraq’s aspirations to boost commerce, energy cooperation, and infrastructure projects with its neighbors.

The Syrian government has not issued an official warning, and IraqiNews.com has not independently confirmed the statements ascribed to the Syrian military source.

However, the claims reflect rising regional worry that strikes by Iran-backed militias operating from Iraqi soil could further destabilize the area and hamper Iraq’s diplomatic and economic goals.

World.title: Iran-backed militias threaten Iraq’s ties with US and Gulf
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Escalating tensions between Iran-backed militias are providing one of the most serious hurdles yet to Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s ambitions to deepen ties with the United States and Gulf states while luring billions of dollars in international investment.

The most recent crisis followed US-Saudi airstrikes on Iran-aligned armed groups in Iraq, when Saudi Arabia accused militias operating from Iraqi territory of firing drones at oil installations in the kingdom’s Eastern Province.

Riyadh claimed that the operation targeted the militias responsible for the assaults rather than the Iraqi state or its military forces, but Baghdad denounced the strikes as a breach of national sovereignty.

The recent tensions are being fueled by numerous prominent Iran-aligned organizations operating inside Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), notably Kataib Hezbollah, Asaib Ahl al-Haq, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada.

While the PMF is technically part of Iraq’s security apparatus, many of its groups have strong links to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and have occasionally conducted operations outside of Baghdad’s chain of command.

Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi responded by calling an emergency meeting of the Ministerial Council for National Security, canceling a planned trip to Saudi Arabia, and announcing a comprehensive security strategy to prevent Iraqi territory from being used to launch attacks on neighboring countries.

The administration also reiterated its resolve to keep all weapons entirely under state control.

That vow has gained importance after Al-Zaidi’s visit to Washington earlier this month, during which Iraq and the United States reiterated their commitment to completing the US-led coalition operation by the end of September 2026.

During the visit, Al-Zaidi pledged to ensure that all weapons eventually come into the control of the Iraqi state, citing it as a cornerstone of his government’s security strategy and a crucial step toward bolstering Iraq’s sovereignty and stability.

Since entering office, Al-Zaidi has maintained a policy of balancing Iraq’s ties with rival regional and international forces.

During recent travels to Washington, Ankara, and Tehran, he achieved huge investment and cooperation deals totaling tens of billions of dollars in the energy, banking, technology, infrastructure, and industrial sectors.

His administration has also attempted to strengthen connections with Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Turkey, and other Gulf nations via new transportation corridors, energy alliances, and trade agreements aimed at diversifying Iraq’s economy beyond oil and positioning the country as a regional center linking the Gulf to Europe.

According to analysts, Baghdad’s approach is highly dependent on proving that the Iraqi state, rather than armed groups, controls the country’s security and foreign policy.

Continued strikes from Iraqi territory risk eroding the country’s reputation with major regional allies and international investors, at a time when foreign investment has risen after years of turmoil.

The stakes rose when US President Donald Trump said that recent US-Saudi operations against Iran-backed militias were coordinated with the Iraqi government, a claim Baghdad has denied.

Observers believe it reflects rising discontent among Iraq’s leadership with armed groups accused of dragging the nation into regional conflicts that contradict Baghdad’s diplomatic and economic interests.

Al-Zaidi is currently facing the most significant test of his leadership.

Delivering on his promise to place all weapons under state control will be critical not only for Iraq’s internal security but also for maintaining trust with the United States, Gulf Arab states, and international investors, many of whom support many of the country’s largest economic projects.

Baghdad’s dilemma now extends beyond managing ties between Washington and Tehran.

It demonstrates that the Iraqi state possesses both the authority and the political will to prevent Iran-backed militias from using Iraqi territory to launch attacks that risk isolating the country, harming relations with Arab neighbors and the United States, and jeopardizing Iraq’s long-term economic recovery and investment goals.

World.title: Iraq faces growing fiscal strain
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is under increasing financial strain as plummeting oil earnings tighten government budgets, with Health Minister Abdul Hussein al-Mousawi saying that ensuring monthly public-sector wages has become the government’s top priority.

Speaking at a public meeting, al-Mousawi stated that the government requires approximately 10.8 trillion Iraqi dinars ($8.2 billion) per month to pay public-sector salaries, while current monthly oil revenues have fallen to approximately 2.5 trillion dinars, highlighting the growing gap between government obligations and income.

The statements are one of the most direct public acknowledgements by a top Iraqi official of the government’s financial challenges after months of decreased oil prices and fewer export profits.

Iraq’s government finances remain very vulnerable to variations in global energy markets because the vast bulk of public revenue comes from crude oil.

Official figures published this week indicated that oil accounted for over 84% of federal income in the first five months of 2026, but collections decreased by more than one-third compared to the same time the previous year as oil prices and export profits plummeted.

The health minister also warned of financing restrictions in the healthcare sector, citing worries about the supply of medications and the government’s capacity to sustain public services if financial pressures continue.

The fresh warnings follow weeks of increased regional tensions, which disrupted oil markets and added uncertainty to Iraq’s economic prospects.

As OPEC’s second-largest producer, Iraq relies on oil exports to fund wages, pensions, social welfare, and the majority of government expenditure, making the budget susceptible to long-term reductions in crude prices.

Economists have long cautioned that Iraq’s reliance on oil income makes the nation susceptible to external shocks, while a hefty public-sector pay bill constrains the government’s budgetary flexibility.

Previous administrations attempted to diversify income streams via tax changes and non-oil investments, but hydrocarbons remain the economy’s backbone.

The financial pressure comes at a critical time for Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s government, which has been promoting Iraq as a destination for billions of dollars in foreign investment following agreements signed with US, Turkish, and international companies in energy, banking, technology, and infrastructure.

Continued budgetary strain may make it more urgent to accelerate economic reforms, raise non-oil income, and improve public financial management to lessen Iraq’s reliance on petroleum exports.

They also emphasize that preserving investor trust will be contingent on the government’s ability to maintain macroeconomic stability while continuing to fund big development projects.

Despite the present issues, Iraq has large foreign currency reserves, which act as a financial cushion for the government.

However, experts warn that while reserves might help absorb short-term shocks, they are not a substitute for the fundamental changes needed to diversify the economy and reduce its dependence on unpredictable oil earnings.

World.title: Iraq expects record 22 million pilgrims for Arbaeen
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is prepared to welcome around 22 million pilgrims for this year’s Arbaeen pilgrimage, including up to 5 million overseas tourists, in what officials believe to be one of the country’s greatest religious gatherings and a significant boost to tourism and the local economy.

According to Iraqi official data, well over 22 million people are anticipated to attend the annual pilgrimage to the holy city of Karbala, with 4.5 million to 5 million pilgrims coming from outside Iraq.

The government has announced that tens of thousands of volunteers would be deployed to assist pilgrims, and Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has urged officials to boost the number of buses and other transport services to facilitate travel during the festival.

The surge of foreign tourists is projected to have a substantial impact on Iraq’s tourism, hospitality, transportation, and retail industries, with hotels, restaurants, transit operators, and local businesses benefitting from increased demand during the pilgrimage season.

Officials have extended transportation networks in preparation for this year’s pilgrimage, including more rail services, buses, and logistical assistance, as part of larger measures to boost connectivity and promote Iraq’s tourist industry.

The government has increasingly highlighted religious tourism as a crucial pillar of economic diversification, with millions of people visiting the country’s holy sites at Karbala, Najaf, Kadhimiya, and Samarra each year.

According to officials, continuing investment in infrastructure and tourist services will help Iraq become one of the Middle East’s major religious tourism destinations, while also creating jobs and helping local economies around the country.

World.title: Reports: Iraq PM threatened to resign over militia disarmament
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi has threatened to resign if Iran-aligned armed groups do not cooperate with his government’s efforts to bring all weapons under state control, according to reports citing political sources, highlighting the growing pressure on Baghdad to address one of its most difficult security challenges.

According to sources, Al-Zaidi warned leaders of Iraq’s Shi’ite Coordination Framework that if armed groups did not react to government efforts to disarm and completely submit to state authority, he would stand down.

IraqiNews.com was unable to independently verify the claims, and the Prime Minister’s office had no immediate response.

According to the sources, Al-Zaidi has been more dissatisfied by what he sees as a lack of cooperation on one of his administration’s fundamental commitments: guaranteeing that all weapons stay solely under the control of the Iraqi government.

The claims came days after US-Saudi airstrikes struck Iran-backed groups in Iraq in response to drone assaults on Saudi oil installations, which Riyadh said were launched from Iraqi territory.

The bombings forced Al-Zaidi to call an emergency security conference, cancel a planned trip to Saudi Arabia, and unveil a new security strategy aimed at preventing Iraqi territory from being used to launch attacks on neighboring nations.

Armed organizations have emerged as one of Al-Zaidi’s most pressing problems.

Since entering office, he has attempted to solicit billions of dollars in foreign investment with trips to Washington, Tehran, and Ankara, while portraying Iraq as a stable location for oil, infrastructure, and technological projects.

Analysts believe Baghdad’s economic objectives are strongly dependent on its ability to show that the state, not armed groups, controls Iraq’s security strategy.

Repeated strikes conducted from Iraqi territory have strained ties with regional allies and risk weakening investor trust.

According to Western diplomatic sources published by Asharq Al-Awsat, key Iraqi officials, including Al-Zaidi and members of Iraq’s security apparatus, have received threats in connection with the government’s attempts to restrict weaponry outside of state control.

Unlike many regional leaders, Iraq’s prime minister leads by wide political agreement rather than a legislative majority, restricting his power to make unilateral choices.

Major security and political changes usually need agreement among Iraq’s different political blocs.

Al-Zaidi’s biggest power may not be the threat of resignation, but rather the international backing his administration has garnered as a result of recent accords with the United States, Turkey, and other allies.

These agreements, which span energy, finance, technology, and infrastructure, have boosted hopes that Iraq will attract tens of billions of dollars in investment if security improves.

Whether Al-Zaidi can translate that international momentum into domestic reforms will ultimately depend on gaining broader political support for his pledge to keep all weapons under Iraqi state control, which has become one of his government’s most closely watched tests.

World.title: Iraq denies launching strikes from its territory against neighboring nations
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The military spokesperson for the Iraqi commander-in-chief, Sabah al-Numan, confirmed on Thursday that neither a foreign nor local body has presented proof that recent regional drone attacks were launched from Iraqi territory.

In a statement to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), al-Numan urged accusing parties to submit reliable proof, saying that Baghdad has yet to receive such data.

The development comes following statements made by the Saudi Ministry of Defense, alleging that drone attacks targeting key oil infrastructure in the past few days originated in Iraq.

The Iraqi official indicated that the government will neither tolerate unilateral military acts from within its borders nor accept foreign violations of its territorial sovereignty.

Al-Numan’s remarks come a day after the United States and Saudi Arabia launched coordinated airstrikes targeting several bases of Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), killing and injuring many fighters.

The joint operation targeted several logistical and weapons storage locations in different provinces in Iraq, escalating the current regional battle.

The PMF described the joint US-Saudi strike as a dangerous escalation and a clear breach of Iraqi sovereignty.

World.title: Iraqi oil flows to continue via Turkey’s Ceyhan as renewal deal is discussed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Turkish sources told Reuters that crude oil shipments from northern Iraq to the Turkish port of Ceyhan will continue while the two countries seek an arrangement to extend the pipeline’s operation for another 12 months.

On July 27, a bilateral agreement that had been in place for decades ended. Despite expectations, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi did not sign a 12-month renewal deal during his meeting with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Ankara on Tuesday.

According to a Turkish official, oil flows via the Iraq-Turkey pipeline, which is Baghdad’s only operational export pipeline, will continue while negotiations for a renewal deal are still in progress.

Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar recently announced a 12-month extension agreement between the two countries.

During a joint press conference in Ankara, Erdogan stated on Tuesday that Turkey hopes to finalize a comprehensive energy cooperation agreement as soon as possible.

An extension is intended to provide additional time for discussions on a complete accord. Turkey aims to fully utilize the 1.5 million barrels per day pipeline and consider expanding it to oil fields in southern Iraq.

Turkish data suggests that the pipeline currently transports approximately 170,000 barrels per day.

World.title: Indian diaspora in China flags anti-India social media posts, visa curbs at 1st embassy outreach
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Members of the Indian diaspora in China raised concerns over anti-India content on Chinese social media, declining work visas and employment restrictions for spouses during an Open House hosted by the Indian Embassy in Beijing.

The outreach event, held on Friday, had Indian Ambassador Vikram Doraiswami and senior embassy officials interact with professionals from across sectors on issues affecting the Indian community in China.

Participants flagged what they described as a growing trend of abusive posts targeting Indians, including comments on Indian culture and food habits, besides raising concerns over the declining number of work visas being issued by Chinese authorities and difficulties faced by spouses seeking employment, reported PTI.

Addressing the gathering, Doraiswami said Chinese authorities were aware of the increase in such online content and were taking measures to curb it. He added that the embassy was responding by pushing verified, fact-based information through its official social media channels.

The ambassador also announced that documentation requirements for Chinese citizens applying for Indian visas would be eased from next week to encourage greater travel to India.





Seeking to improve support for the Indian community, the embassy is working on a legal assistance framework for professionals facing workplace-related issues in China and plans to institutionalise the Open House as a regular forum for addressing consular and community concerns.

Doraiswami also said the mission would expand cultural outreach programmes, including events such as the Vasant Mela, to promote India's cultural diversity and cuisine.

The interaction comes amid efforts by New Delhi and Beijing to stabilise bilateral relations, with Doraiswami, who assumed charge in May, stepping up diplomatic engagement with Chinese officials.

World.title: 'Drugs part of enemy nations' terror plan to hurt India': PM Modi during 'Nasha Mukt Yuva' launch - top quotes
World.content:
PM Modi virtually launches 'Nasha Mukt Yuva' campaign (File photo)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Here are the top quotes from his address:

Youth must stay fit for developed India

"Today, all countrymen have come together for a great and important resolve. The campaign we are witnessing is meant for individuals, families and society, but above all, it is for the nation. The campaign, 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat', clearly reflects this resolve. As the country moves towards the goal of a developed India, it is essential that our youth remain physically and mentally healthy and stay away from drugs and other such harmful substances."

"The campaign we are witnessing today is for the individual, the family, and society; above all, it is for the nation. The very name of this movementâthe 'Drug-Free Youth' initiative under the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan â clarifies its resolve. As the nation sets its sights on becoming a Viksit Bharat, it is essential that our youth be healthy in body and mind, brimming with self-confidence, and forever free from the deadly habit of drugs. This is the objective of the campaign... This campaign was launched last year as a pilot project from Kashi... Over 125 spiritual organizations have joined us today for the welfare of crores of our fellow citizens."

"By being addiction-free, you need to protect your potential. You need to be aware that drugs get you high for a short time, but take your career and family to a new low/bottom.

From Varanasi to nationwide campaign

"As the MP from Kashi, I am happy that this campaign was launched last year from the sacred land of Kashi as a pilot project. Along with scientific clarity, it also carries spiritual energy. Social organisations and NGOs have joined this initiative for the welfare of crores of Indians. Together, they have prepared a roadmap through the Kashi Declaration. Today, we are witnessing how the welfare-oriented idea that emerged from Kashi has become a national project. From today, the Nasha Mukt Yuva campaign is being launched across the country."

"The 'Nasha Mukta Yuva Abhiyaan' is launching across the country today... There is immense power in collective action, and today, driven by that very strength, this campaign is set to touch the heart of every young person. Lakhs of youths across the nation took a pledge to stay free from drugs... The pledge taken today will continue to move forward steadily over the next hundred weeks."

"Drug use disturbs focus, takes you away from dreams. If a youth gets addicted to drugs, his aspirations take a hit, family gets shattered."

Govt's anti-drug drive and national campaign

"Today, the government stands firmly with the youth in the campaign against drugs. Strict action is being taken in the country against drug traffickers and drug abuse; there have been many times more arrests compared to before, and drugs worth thousands of crores of rupees have been seized. This shows how tough our government is against drugs."

"Today, thousands of students from schools, colleges and universities are connected online to this programme. Even lakhs of volunteers of MY Bharat are also connected. The NSS jawans too have joined us. People from different sectors, institutions and backgrounds--more than 1 crore youths are together today. I congratulate all of you for this big movement."

Youth key to Viksit Bharat, drugs part of enemy agenda

"You are India's Amrit Peedhi. You will shape your lives over the next 20-25 years, and you will lead the country to the goal of a Viksit Bharat in 2047, and you will be at the helm. You will be the ones to reap its full benefits."

"The country needs your energy, your imagination, and your talent, so staying drug-free is crucial for the country and for your own lives."

"When a young person falls prey to drug addiction, it is not just that individual who loses; a dream is lost. Hostile nations conspire and leave no stone unturned to drag our youth into the trap of addiction. Profiting from the supply of drugs while aiming to destroy a country like ours is part of their terror-driven agenda."

Parents, teachers and society must lead the fight

"We must always keep this in mind: if any child from our home has become a victim of addiction, do not hide it under the guise of social prestige. Seek help from whoever is needed."

"Make efforts to free your child from addiction with medical help."

"We should also foster a culture of open communication with children in the family, so that you can hold their hand before they get caught in such a whirlpool."

"Along with teaching the courses, please also discuss the dangers of drugs with the students. Launch a movement against addiction on your campus. Your efforts can bring big results."

"The support of society, the power of yoga and meditation--these strengthen our inner resolve against addiction. And today, we also have facilities like rehabilitation centres to help quit drugs."

"I appeal to all of you that you are all the leaders of this great movement. You have further strengthened my belief that the youth of India is so aware, so sensible, and so serious about their duties."

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday launched the 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan', calling on the country's youth to stay physically and mentally fit and remain away from drug abuse.He said achieving the goal of a developed India requires a healthy, confident and drug-free younger generation. During his address, PM Modi also highlighed how the drugs affect one's family and career.Launching the campaign through video conferencing, PM Modi said the initiative is not only for individuals, families and society but also for the nation. He added that the next 100 Sundays would represent 100 strong steps towards a drug-free India."Next 100 Sundays will mark 100 strong steps towards drug-free India," he said.PM Modi also warned that drug trafficking was part of a larger strategy by hostile forces to weaken India and called for greater public vigilance. "Hurting India's interests by supplying drugs part of enemy nations' terror plan," he said.The 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan' aims to encourage young people to stay away from substance abuse and become ambassadors of positive social change in their communities.The launch marks the beginning of a 100-week nationwide Jan Bhagidari campaign, under which awareness programmes will be organised every Sunday across the country.Activities will include sports events, walkathons, meditation sessions, cultural programmes, street plays, discussions, art competitions and community engagement initiatives.The campaign brings together educational institutions, youth organisations, civil society groups, industry bodies and more than 125 spiritual organisations to build a collective movement against substance abuse.Youth from over 10,000 locations across the country are participating through schools, colleges, universities, MY Bharat volunteers, NSS volunteers, youth clubs, NGOs and industry associations.

World.title: 'Let Cauvery unite our people': Karnataka BJP chief calls on Tamil Nadu CM Vijay to bridge 'differences'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Karnataka BJP president BY Vijayendra has written to

Vijay, urging him to adopt a cooperative approach to the long-running

and support the proposed Mekedatu reservoir project, saying the river should 'unite our people, rather than divide them.'

The appeal comes amid renewed tensions between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu after the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) directed Karnataka to release 3,500 cusecs of water per day to Tamil Nadu for 15 days.

The direction has triggered protests in Karnataka, while the DMK has moved the Supreme Court seeking implementation of the water release order and clearance of the accumulated shortfall.

In his letter, Vijayendra said differences between neighbouring states were natural but should be resolved through dialogue and statesmanship.

"As neighbouring states, differences are inevitable. What matters is how we resolve them," he wrote.

Referring to the earlier resolution of the dispute over the Thiruvalluvar statue in Bengaluru, Vijayendra said former Karnataka chief minister BS Yediyurappa and former Tamil Nadu chief minister M Karunanidhi had demonstrated that difficult issues could be settled when larger public interest prevailed.

"Their maturity demonstrated that even difficult issues can be resolved when the larger interests of our people prevail.





That is the spirit in which I appeal to you today," he wrote.

The Karnataka BJP chief said the Cauvery was a lifeline for crores of people in Bengaluru and several towns across the Cauvery basin, including both Kannadigas and Tamilians living in Karnataka.

"At a time when inadequate and erratic monsoons have placed enormous stress on farmers and citizens alike, their concerns cannot be overlooked," he said.

Vijayendra also urged Vijay to reconsider Karnataka's proposed Mekedatu reservoir project, saying it would help meet Bengaluru's drinking water needs without affecting Tamil Nadu's legitimate share of Cauvery waters.

"I also appeal to you to view the Mekedatu project in the spirit of cooperation. It can significantly address Bengaluru's drinking-water requirements without compromising the legitimate water needs of Tamil Nadu," he wrote.

"Your support for the project can become a powerful symbol of cooperation between our two states."

He expressed hope that Vijay would take a 'statesmanlike position' that protected Karnataka's interests while respecting those of Tamil Nadu.

"I sincerely hope you will take a statesmanlike position that protects Karnataka's genuine interests while respecting those of Tamil Nadu, and help strengthen the historic bond between our two states. Let the Cauvery unite our people, rather than divide them," the letter said.

Poll Vote & Share your view Should Karnataka and Tamil Nadu prioritize dialogue over disputes? Absolutely, dialogue is key. Not necessarily, some disputes require legal action. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

What is the Cauvery water dispute?

The Cauvery water dispute is one of India's longest-running inter-state river disputes involving Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry.

It centres on the sharing of the Cauvery river, which is a major source of drinking water and irrigation for millions of people.

The Supreme Court's 2018 judgment largely upheld the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal's water-sharing formula and led to the creation of the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) and the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) to oversee implementation.

Tamil Nadu has opposed the project, arguing that it could affect its allocated share of Cauvery waters and violate the existing water-sharing framework.

NEW DELHI: Want to age more slowly? The answer may lie not just in exercise and diet, but also in a trip to the theatre, museum or even the cinema.A new study by Japanese researchers has found that older adults who engage more frequently in cultural activities tend to have a lower physiological ageâa measure of how well the body's organs and systems are functioningâthan their actual age, suggesting cultural engagement may be an overlooked tool for healthy ageing.Researchers from the Institute of Science Tokyo analysed 4,207 observations from 1,899 adults aged 50 years and above in the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing. Participants who more frequently visited cinemas, museums, art galleries, theatres, concerts or the opera had lower physiological age. Every one-point increase in cultural engagement score was associated with a 0.085-year reduction in physiological age, even after adjusting for income, health status, employment, smoking, physical activity and other factors. The association persisted in a four-year follow-up analysis. Physiological age, estimated using 10 markers including blood pressure, lung function, grip strength, walking speed, BMI, haemoglobin, cholesterol and blood sugar, is considered a better predictor of disease and mortality than chronological age.The researchers said cultural engagement may promote healthy ageing by strengthening social connections, reducing loneliness and stress, improving mental well-being and encouraging healthier lifestyles.Indian experts said the findings reinforce the importance of staying socially engaged as people age.Dr Prasun Chatterjee, Group Clinical Lead, Department of Geriatric Medicine and Longevity Sciences, Apollo Hospitals, and former professor at AIIMS, said the findings reinforce that healthy ageing depends not only on diet and exercise but also on social and cultural engagement. Social interaction improves memory and mood by boosting serotonin and dopamine, enhancing emotional well-being, memory and a sense of purpose, which encourage healthier lifestyles. In the Indian context, he said, activities such as visiting parks, cinemas, theatres or places of worship can provide similar benefits by promoting happiness, social connection and purpose.Prof Rajesh Sagar, psychiatrist at AIIMS, New Delhi, said social and cultural engagement promotes healthy ageing by strengthening emotional support networks, improving cognitive function and reducing chronic stress.He said loneliness increases the risk of depression, anxiety and cognitive decline while reducing motivation for physical activity. He advised older adults to stay socially connected by regularly meeting friends and relatives or joining walking groups, book clubs, music classes or spiritual gatherings.The authors cautioned that the study shows an association, not causation, as healthier people may also be more likely to participate in cultural activities. World.title: Global breastfeeding rates rise, India yet to arrest decline
World.content:
File photo

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Even as exclusive breastfeeding rates have improved globally over the past decade, India continues to lag behind, with the proportion of infants exclusively breastfed for the first six months declining from 63.7% in NFHS-5 (2019-21) to 55.8% in NFHS-6 (2023-24).Ahead of World Breastfeeding Week (August 1-7), the World Health Organization (WHO) and UNICEF called for stronger support systems for mothers, saying global exclusive breastfeeding has increased from about 37% in 2012 to over 47% today, driven by sustained investments in health systems, community counselling and maternity protection. However, the agencies said progress remains uneven and many countries continue to fall short of global targets.Responding to a question in the Rajya Sabha, the Union health ministry attributed the decline in India's exclusive breastfeeding rate to multiple factors, including socio-cultural practices, family customs, individual preferences, the use of pre-lacteal feeds and infant milk substitutes, and breastfeeding frequency.The ministry, however, highlighted improvements in other breastfeeding indicators.Early initiation of breastfeeding within one hour of birth increased from 41.8% to 50.1%, while the proportion of infants below six months receiving any breast milk rose marginally from 95.1% to 95.6%.The Rajya Sabha question had sought to know whether the government had assessed the impact of rising Caesarean deliveries, inadequate postnatal lactation counselling and early return to work, particularly among women in the informal sector. While the ministry did not provide findings of any such assessment, it said the National Health Mission promotes exclusive breastfeeding through the Mother Absolute Affection (MAA) programme, lactation management centres, healthcare worker training, Poshan Tracker-based counselling and community awareness campaigns.It also cited a 2025 NITI Aayog evaluation, which found that new mothers were receiving information on exclusive breastfeeding during the postnatal period.Calling breastfeeding one of the most effective public health interventions, WHO and UNICEF said it provides essential nutrition, protects children against infections, strengthens immunity, supports cognitive development and lowers mothers' risk of breast and ovarian cancers and type 2 diabetes. The agencies said scaling up proven interventions, including skilled breastfeeding support, community counselling, paid maternity leave, supportive workplace policies and stronger regulation of breast-milk substitute marketing, could prevent nearly 400,000 child deaths and 140,000 maternal deaths globally every year.

World.title: Sarnath earns UNESCO World Heritage tag, takes India’s tally to 45
World.content:
The ancient Buddhist site of Sarnath in Varanasi was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List during the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee, held in Busan, South Korea. The announcement was made by the committee’s chairperson, Lee Byong Hyun, at the annual conclave on Sunday.

Sarnath recognised as UNESCO World Heritage Site: Full list of India's sites, criteria for inclusion

With the inscription of Sarnath, India now has 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

The Uttar Pradesh site has been recognised as a serial property comprising the Chaukhandi Stupa and the Archaeological Remains of Sarnath, which include the preserved archaeological and architectural remains of the ancient Buddhist site.

Sarnath is believed to be the place where Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon after attaining enlightenment in the 6th century BCE. Also known as Rishipatana, Ishipatana, Mrigadava or the Deer Park, it is regarded as the sacred site where the Buddha met his first disciples, who later spread his teachings on peace and the nature of suffering.

A proud moment for every Indian!



Delighted that Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh has been inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.



Sarnath has a close association with Lord Buddha, whose timeless message of wisdom, compassion and harmony inspires the world.



This recognition… https://t.co/KkdMOg6g0d — Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) July 25, 2026

Reacting to the development, Prime Minister Narendra Modi took to X and posted: “...This recognition celebrates India’s profound civilisational and spiritual heritage. It will also inspire more people across the world to come to Sarnath and connect with the ideals of Lord Buddha.”

Explaining the inscription, UNESCO said, “Sarnath, Varanasi bears witness to the enduring spiritual significance of Sarnath, one of the four principal destinations of Buddhist pilgrimage, established by the Buddha himself, as demonstrated by the large number of religious buildings and other monuments that were built and rebuilt on-site during the many centuries of its existence.”

World.title: Forest Department starts collating all illegally geo-tagged locations in Kerala forests
World.content:
The Forest Department has decided to take stock of all locations in Kerala’sforests that have been illegally geo-tagged by individuals on online map platforms. The Kerala Forest Department’s IT wing is collating a list of these locations, which will then be forwarded to the Forest Management Wing.

It is learnt that the department will submit the final list to online map agencies and platforms, seeking the removal of these locations from the maps. Moreover, the department plans to identify the individuals who uploaded these locations within the reserve and protected forest areas and initiate legal action.

Geo-tagging these sensitive locations on web mapping and navigation platforms is leading to unlawful entry into reserve forests, said a Forest official.

“Even trekking trails used by forest staff inside protected forest patches in Silent Valley to the camp sheds, etc., have been made available on online maps. These are sensitive locations and information. We believe this could have been put up by the volunteers who must have come to assist us in any of the wildlife census programmes,” said the official. Knowing that the move endangers humans as well as wildlife, the official added that strict action will be taken against those involved. “Forests are not places you can randomly picnic at. These are the homes of wild animals and hey need to be respected,” the official added.

Earlier, Kozhikode Divisional Forest Officer M. Joshil had sought the removal of Google Maps listings inside reserve forests in the district. Noting that these were unauthorised map pins and that the uploaded photographs are encouraging illegal entry into protected areas, he had taken up the issue with the Department’s IT wing.

Following this, the forest department initiated the move to take note of all such locations in Kerala forests.

“Such activities put everyone at risk. Of late, we have been dealing with many such cases of illegal entry of individuals into the forests and eventually carrying out the subsequent rescue activities when they get trapped. It can lead to human-Wildlife conflict due to someone else’s irresponsible behaviour,” said Mr. Joshil.

Shivakumar and former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and DMK president M.K. Stalin’s family shared a cordial relationship that went beyond politics, Mr. Nirmalkumar said that Mr. Shivakumar wanted the DMK to return to power and the Karnataka CM would listen to the DMK leader’s family rather than the Congress leadership.

In such a situation, he alleged, the DMK had hurriedly filed a separate petition before the Supreme Court.

According to him, multiple petitions filed on behalf of the same State before the Supreme Court would create confusion and affect the State’s rights. He also questioned how many petitions the DMK had filed on the Cauvery issue during the past five years.

World.title: Weaponising extraordinary laws to silence dissent: Congress on rights activist held under NSA in Assam
World.content:
The Congress on Sunday (August 2, 2026) slammed the Assam government over indigenous rights activist Pranab Doley being detained under the National Security Act, alleging that the use of the NSA against him was part of a growing pattern of BJP governments "weaponising" extraordinary laws to silence dissent.

The Opposition party also said this is a "blatant misuse" of preventive detention laws and "overreach" by the State.

Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh said that on July 30, the Assam Government invoked the National Security Act (NSA) against land rights activist Doley, just a day after the district court granted him bail.

"This is a blatant misuse of preventive detention laws and overreach by the state," Ramesh said on X.

Mr. Doley has been arrested for supporting villagers who protested against a proposed five-star resort near the Kaziranga National Park that the Assam Chief Minister had backed, he said.

Since 2022, indigenous residents of Golaghat have protested and even petitioned the Gauhati High Court against the project, arguing the land was forcibly acquired from them, Mr. Ramesh said.

On 30 July, the Assam Government invoked the National Security Act (NSA) against land rights activist Pranab Doley, just a day after the District Court granted him bail. This is a blatant misuse of preventive detention laws and overreach by the state.



Doley has been arrested for… — Jairam Ramesh (@Jairam_Ramesh) August 2, 2026

While granting him bail on July 29, the sessions court had observed that "where ecological preservation intersects with indigenous survival, criminal law cannot be used to suppress legitimate local anxieties", Mr. Ramesh said.

It is clear that the Assam government invoked the NSA to do exactly that, he alleged.

“Doley's NSA detention order relies on vague and speculative allegations, including that Doley had engaged in ‘suspicious foreign transactions from doubtful sources’, which is the Modi government's familiar script,” the Congress leader said.

"The use of the NSA against Doley is part of a growing pattern of BJP governments weaponising extraordinary laws to silence dissent," Mr. Ramesh said.

Similar attempts have been witnessed in Uttar Pradesh, where the NSA was invoked against labour activists protesting against exploitative working conditions in Noida, he said.

BJP governments across the country cannot suppress legitimate grievances of working-class, indigenous, and marginalised communities through arrests and draconian laws, he said.

"The Assam Government continues to show utter disregard for the rule of law and for democratic dissent. The Supreme Court and several high courts have repeatedly cautioned that preventive detention laws must not be used as a device to defeat or circumvent judicial orders granting bail, or merely to prolong a person's incarceration," the Congress leader said.

His remarks come after Mr. Doley was detained under the stringent NSA, a day after securing bail in a case related to protests against a proposed five-star hotel near Kaziranga National Park in Assam.

Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi, criticising the move on Saturday, maintained that it shows the state government does not allow dissent, as he also mentioned Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma "threatening" to use NSA against artists over a mural of singer Zubeen Garg in Guwahati.

Mr. Doley, who was arrested in Guwahati on July 13 and lodged in Golaghat district jail, was granted bail by a court on Wednesday in connection with the June protest.

However, the State government invoked the NSA against him on Thursday, ensuring his continued detention in the same jail, according to the order.

The order issued by the Political (A) Department said the government was satisfied that Doley's activities were "prejudicial to the maintenance of public order as well as security of the state" and that there was a "real and imminent possibility" of him continuing such activities if released.

Stating that preventive detention was necessary, the order, issued under Section 3(2) of the NSA, 1980, directed that Doley be detained and kept in custody at the Golaghat District Jail.

Mr. Doley has been spearheading protests against the proposed five-star hotel near the UNESCO World Heritage Site Kaziranga National Park, alleging that the project poses a threat to the area's fragile ecology.

A peasants' rights activist, Doley had also unsuccessfully contested the April assembly elections from the Bokakhat constituency against AGP president Atul Bora, a State cabinet minister.

World.title: Day after securing bail, Assam activist Pranab Doley detained under NSA
World.content:
Amid ongoing protests in Assam over a luxury hotel project near the Kaziranga National Park, the Government of Assam has now invoked the National Security Act (NSA) to detain environmental activist Pranab Doley, who has been supporting and leading these protests for weeks now.

Weaponising extraordinary laws to silence dissent: Congress on rights activist held under NSA in Assam

Mr. Doley was arrested by the police in Assam on July 12 over a sit-in protest that was held in the area and was granted bail by a local court earlier this week on July 29. The court, while granting him bail, had observed in the order, “In matters where ecological preservation intersects with indigenous survival, the standard apparatus of criminal law cannot be used to suppress local anxieties.”

In an order issued the day after Mr. Doley was granted bail, the Political Department of the Assam Government said his activities were “prejudicial to the maintenance of public order as well as security of the State”, adding that the government was invoking powers under the National Security Act, 1980 to preventively detain him.

‘Foreign funding’

Further, in a notification accompanying the NSA detention order, which laid out the grounds for his detention, the Assam Government has cited as many as 13 police cases registered against Mr. Doley from as far back as 2017; it alleged that he had received funding from foreign sources and that he had made several trips to foreign countries like Spain, Italy, Thailand, UAE, Nepal, Norway, Phillippines, Switzerland, and Malaysia.

The Assam Government went ahead and accused Mr. Doley of being involved in “road blockades and damage of public properties with an intent to create lawlessness for personal and vested interests”. Among the police cases cited by the State government, it specifically said Mr. Doley had been accused of “offences against women, public servants, hate incitement”, among others, including the latest FIR in July this month, over which he was arrested.

In this latest FIR over the protests near the site of the proposed hotel project, the Assam police accused Mr. Doley and other activists and leaders of inciting protesters to act unlawfully, instigating the protesters to attack police personnel and allegedly outrage the modesty of women police personnel, among other charges.

While granting bail, the court of the Additional Sessions Judge in Golaghat concluded that the police were unable to seize any “deadly weapons” from the protesters as alleged, adding that available video material from the protest also did not show any deadly weapons. The court further noted that there was no video material to show any male protester attacking or outraging the modesty of women police personnel.

The court also examined arguments of the Assam police that Mr. Doley should be denied bail because of his foreign “connections”, visits, and funding. The Assam Government had added that Mr. Doley had also received funding from an organisation currently being investigated by the Central Bureau of Investigation for alleged violations of the FCRA.

The court noted that none of Mr. Doley’s foreign visits or funding seems to be hidden, adding that the CBI probe was still ongoing and did not indicate any illegal role of Mr. Doley himself.

Before parting with the order, Additional Sessions Judge N.M. Abdullah Ahmed noted that the nature of the issue in this case was a result of a “deep-rooted anxiety regarding environmental degradation and its impact on the socio-cultural fabric of the local Tea Tribes”. He went on to say that in such cases, “treating the activists or community leaders as ‘external disruptive element’ will not yield any fruitful result in the long run”.

World.title: Krishna water releases: YSRCP criticises government policy
World.content:
YSRCP general secretary and former vice-chairman of the Andhra Pradesh State Agriculture Mission M.V.S. Nagi Reddy has accused the State government of failing to utilise available Krishna River water to support irrigation in drought-prone regions and the Krishna delta.
